📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla has started rolling out “Full Self-Driving” v15, and its list of improvements reads like a list of FSD’s biggest current weaknesses: sign detection, potholes, and speed handling in school zones.

Tesla also claims “25x better handling of safety critical cases” and is adding a latest live visualization that looks seriously impressive. If the driving improvements are as real as the visuals, this is a substantial patch.

It has been revealed that tesla announced the rollout on X this afternoon, and its Tesla Super Intelligence account followed up with the full release notes. The company didn’t say which vehicles get it first, but it has previously told investors that its AI4 (HW4) computer is enough to run v15.

Here are Tesla’s release notes for FSD v15:.

v15 upgrades every part of the end-to-end driving network. Includes:.

Industry observers note that tesla’s main announcement also says FSD can now slow down for speed cameras, and it adds Bike Rack Mode, which allows FSD with a bike rack or a similar hitch accessory. Navigation learning only covers the start and end of trips for now; Tesla says later v15 releases will expand it to the entire route.

The newly introduced visualization is the flashiest part, and based on the video Tesla shared, it’s super impressive. The center screen shows a detailed, rendered version of the street around the car, far beyond the current FSD visualization.

FSD v15 now starting to roll out – upgrading every part of the end-to-end driving network Safety25x better handling of safety critical casesTesla Reality View Adds a live visualization of the drive that lets you see & control what FSD is planning to doNavigation for start… pic.twitter.com/Sfjk4wZecW.

Tesla calls it “Reality View” in its announcement and “Tesla Augmented Reality” in the release notes. The notes say it replaces all the separate model signals with a single end-to-end visualization that uses less compute, and Tesla says it lets the driver “see & control what FSD is planning to do.” If that works as advertised, it could make supervising the system a lot easier.

According to recent reports, what stands out more is where Tesla is focusing. Almost every driving improvement in the release notes targets an area where FSD struggles today.

Industry observers note that signs are a major one. In a test published in September, Brussels nonprofit Johanna.be found that FSD exceeded the limit in 55% of the 30 km/h zones it drove through, averaging 44 km/h. In most of those zones, the car’s screen demonstrated a 50 km/h limit. It didn’t read the sign.

In a recent development, potholes are another. In August, Musk remarked pothole avoidance was “coming soon”, something he had already promised back in 2019. Today, FSD still drives straight through them.

Industry observers note that school zones are on the list too. NHTSA is reviewing a petition claiming Tesla’s Robotaxis speed through active school zones, on top of an investigation it opened in October 2025 into FSD traffic-law violations like running red lights. Slowing for speed cameras fits the same theme, though it also suggests Tesla is fine with FSD going over the limit when there’s no camera around.

So if v15 really fixes these, it’s a very good revision. The question is by how much.

Recent findings suggest that one change goes the other way. Tesla states it is “decreasing strictness” of driver monitoring in higher-speed driver profiles, at a time when sleeping drivers on FSD keep making headlines and Tesla is tightening monitoring in Europe at regulators’ request.

The release notes clear up what the “25x” refers to: Tesla says the fresh vision encoder improves the critical intervention rate by 25x. That’s the right metric to measure progress toward unsupervised driving. But Tesla still doesn’t share the actual number, only the multiplier.

It has been revealed that the math gets interesting fast. Our data from earlier this year suggested FSD v14 could go a couple thousand miles between critical interventions. A 25x improvement on that would put v15 around 50,000 miles between critical interventions, well beyond the roughly 10,000 miles we’ve mentioned Tesla needs for a limited unsupervised service. If that were true across the fleet, we could see Tesla having its most meaningful push toward autonomy in a long time.

And v15 already carries plenty of hype. In April, Elon Musk wrote that v15 “will far exceed human levels of safety, even in completely unsupervised and complex situations.” We pointed out at the time that he had said similar things about v12 and v14. In August, Tesla told JPMorgan that v15 is a “step-change” built on seven “core technologies,” with about 40% of them already running in its Robotaxi fleet in Austin.

Sources indicate that FSD has never improved in a straight line. Every major version has brought real gains along with fresh problems, and point releases regularly go backward.

When v14 arrived in October 2025, it came with hallucinations, brake stabbing, and excessive speeding, and early crowdsourced data revealed about 732 miles between critical disengagements, below what we expected. It then improved a lot. Then the v14.2 updates went backward before Musk sold v14.3 as the version where “the last big piece of the puzzle finally lands.”.

Seven months and a long string of point releases later, owners are still supervising, and Tesla now needs v15 to deliver what v14.3 was supposed to.

I remain skeptic of Tesla's autonomous driving until they apply for the California DMV permit to begin testing autonomous driving without a driver. California is a massive enough of a potential market for robotaxi that Tesla is operating a human driver taxi service. The common presumption is that Tesla is avoiding California autonomous testing because it requires disclosing critical interventions and other data which wouldn't be favorable to Tesla's claims.

The visuals are super impressive. That much we can already judge from the video, and Reality View could make FSD easier to understand and supervise.

The driving side is harder to judge. Tesla is going straight at the weaknesses that owners and regulators complain about most: misread speed limits, potholes, school zones, debris. If v15 delivers real progress on all of those, it’s a really good patch.

Sources indicate that but “improved detection” doesn’t tell us how much better, and a 25x multiplier without the underlying number is hard to check. FSD has gone two steps forward, one step back throughout its history, with point releases regularly breaking things the previous version handled fine. And Tesla still won’t publish the disengagement data that would settle it.

2027 Toyota Sienna Drive: More than Meets the Eye

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1064 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Caranddriver

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most mid-cycle refreshes touch only the surface stuff: a latest grille, new headlights, new wheel designs.
  • Much like a person who is very bad at seeing those magic-eye illusions, you could stare at a picture of the 2027 Sienna all day and nothing new would make itself apparent.
  • Industry observers note that the base LE loses its 8.0-inch infotainment screen as Toyota democratizes digital real estate, granting every Sienna a 12.3-inch infotainment screen and a 12.3-inch gauge display.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most mid-cycle refreshes touch only the surface stuff: a latest grille, new headlights, new wheel designs. They typically don’t venture too far into the mechanicals. Toyota flipped the script in its approach to the 2027 Sienna hybrid minivan, mostly leaving the visuals alone and focusing instead on the substantive bits. The result is a minivan that’s more upgraded than it looks.

Much like a person who is very bad at seeing those magic-eye illusions, you could stare at a picture of the 2027 Sienna all day and nothing new would make itself apparent. The exterior is unchanged, although one paint color (Cypress) has been dropped in favor of a new hue (Storm Cloud). The trims have also been rejiggered: The Limited is gone, and the XSE picks up some of its features and becomes the new penultimate trim beneath Platinum. Otherwise, every inch of mid-cycle-refresh effort went into the underlying tech and the powertrain.

See all results for used cars for sale near 10025.

Industry observers note that the base LE loses its 8.0-inch infotainment screen as Toyota democratizes digital real estate, granting every Sienna a 12.3-inch infotainment screen and a 12.3-inch gauge display. Upcoming LED cabin lighting arrives, and the rear-seat entertainment picks up major upgrades with native apps and a new touchscreen. The sound-deadening material behind the dashboard has also been tweaked.

We saved the best bits for last. The 2027 Sienna adopts Toyota’s latest (sixth-gen) hybrid powertrain, which first arrived in the Lexus ES. The old nickel-metal hydride battery is replaced by a lithium-ion pack that stores more energy, and it feeds a redesigned and more efficient electric motor to produce a combined 251 horsepower—six more than its predecessor. All-wheel-drive models energize the rear axle with an additional motor, though that doesn’t raise output any. Toyota estimates a 7.5-second run to 60 mph in front-wheel-drive guise, rising to 7.6 with all-wheel drive (since there’s more mass and no extra oomph). Either way, that’s 0.3 to 0.4 second quicker than the 2026 Sienna. Our long-term 2021 Toyota Sienna Limited AWD did the deed in 7.6 seconds.

Sources indicate that the 2026 Sienna earned EPA fuel-economy estimates of 36 city, 36 highway, and 36 combined for front-wheel-drive models and 35/36/35 for all-wheel-drive variants. While official numbers have not yet been released for the 2027 model, Toyota claims city improvements of 3 mpg (FWD) and 4 mpg (AWD), with combined estimates rising between 1 and 2 mpg.

Recent findings suggest that because these changes might not seem like much on paper, Toyota gave us access to both a 2026 Sienna and a 2027 Sienna to better experience the changes. And we’re glad we had that opportunity, because the revised Sienna does make for a vastly improved driving experience.

See all results for used cars for sale near 10025.

Industry observers note that we liked the 2027 Sienna more before we even pushed the start button. The Sienna’s latest steering wheel puts switches in more sensible locations; it’s much easier to operate on the fly, plus it looks better. The 2026 model’s tech feels a full step behind the 2027 model’s, with its analog gauge cluster (on the lower trims) and tiny info display, or the complete lack of USB-C ports. Thankfully, with the 2027 Sienna’s new tech comes a whole host of electrical-system changes, including a move to USB-C. Our tangled morass of a cable drawer thanks you, Toyota.

In a recent development, in addition to sprinkling better ports around the cabin, the Sienna’s new updated tech also enhances the driving experience. The electronic power steering is lighter at lower road speeds, making around-town navigation slightly less onerous, and it also exhibits better on-center stability at highway speeds, again eliminating some tedium. The brakes also include a feature Toyota calls Vehicle Braking Posture Control, which applies braking to individual wheels to reduce body roll in cornering; after taking both Siennas to our 10Best evaluation loop, we can confirm that the revised Sienna does corner ever so slightly flatter, and you don’t even need to drive like a Car and Driver editor to feel the improvement.

As for the Sienna’s powertrain, we loved it in the latest generation of Lexus ES, and we very much enjoy it here as well. As Toyota promised, the sixth-gen hybrid brings noticeable improvements to noise, vibration, and harshness. In the 2026 model, the combustion engine sounds and feels coarser low in the rev range. In the 2027 model, the powertrain is both smoother and quieter, with an audible reduction in cabin noise (a change we’re excited to get the chance to confirm via testing at a later date). Simply put, driving the 2027 Sienna offers a more serene experience—for both driver and passengers—than you’d find in its predecessor.

Industry observers note that some changes incur massive cost penalties, but the 2027 Sienna doesn't ask too much extra off the top. It's estimated to come in around $44,500 for the base LE model with front-wheel drive. For context, the 2026 Sienna started at $42,915 for the base LE, rising to $60,305 for the top-spec Platinum; the slightly more rugged Woodland Edition was $53,695. Given just how much better the 2027 Sienna drives, we think it’s worth the higher cost of entry.

#109513. Latest Update: Scientists discover that the heart doesn't age the way we thought

Latest Update: Scientists discover that the heart doesn't age the way we thought

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1687 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As the heart gets older, inflammation increases, but scientists have not fully understood where these changes occur or which parts of the organ are most affected.
  • In a recent development, in a study of mouse hearts published in Aging Cell, the researchers discovered that signs of inflammation and tissue scarring were especially concentrated around the aortic valves and aortic root.
  • "Some of the markers associated with inflammaging were there from the very beginning in young hearts, but they were focused specifically in areas no one had defined before, in the valves and the aorta rather than in muscle tissue," remarked study author Nadia Rosenthal, scientific director at JAX.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As the heart gets older, inflammation increases, but scientists have not fully understood where these changes occur or which parts of the organ are most affected. Researchers at The Jackson Laboratory (JAX) have now uncovered a surprising pattern: Certain regions of the heart appear to be hotspots for aging-related inflammation, offering upcoming clues about how the heart changes over time.

In a recent development, in a study of mouse hearts published in Aging Cell, the researchers discovered that signs of inflammation and tissue scarring were especially concentrated around the aortic valves and aortic root. These areas contain immune cells and connective tissue cells whose interactions change with age, potentially affecting the surrounding heart muscle. The findings provide a fresh picture of cardiac aging and could guide future efforts to understand cardiovascular disease.

"Some of the markers associated with inflammaging were there from the very beginning in young hearts, but they were focused specifically in areas no one had defined before, in the valves and the aorta rather than in muscle tissue," remarked study author Nadia Rosenthal, scientific director at JAX. "We really have to think of aging as something that is not linear, because just like we know that people don't age at the same rate, what we know now is that organs and tissues don't age at the same rate either, even within one individual.".

Much of the previous research on heart aging has centered on cardiac muscle, particularly the left ventricle. This chamber performs the essential task of pumping blood into the aorta and throughout the body. By studying the heart as a whole, rather than concentrating primarily on its muscle, the JAX team uncovered important changes in other tissues and the ways their cells interact.

"The valves and the major blood vessels are parts often thought of as plumbing rather than the main engine, but this is a very complicated little machine," Rosenthal mentioned. "It turns out they're home to many of the cells we're interested in, and that's where some of the most important aging-related signals were concentrated.".

Mapping Hidden Hotspots of Heart Aging.

Growing older is the single greatest risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet many of the cellular processes responsible for the heart's decline remain poorly understood. One challenge is that mammalian heart muscle cells have very little ability to regenerate or replace themselves. To investigate what happens as the heart ages, Rosenthal and her colleagues used advanced techniques that allowed them to study thousands of individual cells from young and old mice while also identifying their locations within the heart.

Scientists already know that aging is accompanied by a persistent, low level of inflammation throughout the body. Earlier studies have found similar changes in the heart, including an increase in immune cells that regulate inflammatory activity (macrophages) and cells that produce and maintain connective tissue and contribute to scar formation (fibroblasts).

According to recent reports, the newly introduced analysis indicated that aging macrophages became more active in genes involved in inflammation and changes to tissue structure. Fibroblasts, meanwhile, increasingly displayed molecular characteristics associated with fibrosis (or scarring). Crucially, the researchers went beyond identifying which genes were active. They also mapped the locations of these cells, making it possible to see how different regions of the heart change as they grow older.

It has been revealed that this approach revealed that inflammation and fibrosis (or scarring) were not distributed uniformly. Instead, the strongest signals appeared around the heart valves and aortic root. The researchers believe these regions may act as important centers of cardiac aging, where changes in supporting cells could influence the health of nearby heart muscle.

"To keep muscle cells happy, the other cells in the heart have to continue supporting them throughout life," Rosenthal stated. "What this study does, for the first time, is provide a comprehensive picture of how those support cells, particularly fibroblasts and macrophages, change with age and contribute to what we call inflammaging.".

Surprising Signs of Aging in Young Hearts.

Another unexpected discovery challenged assumptions about how scientists identify aging cells. The team examined molecular markers frequently associated with cellular senescence, a state in which cells permanently lose the ability to divide, often because of aging or stress. As senescent cells accumulate, they can contribute to ongoing inflammation, tissue damage, and diseases associated with older age.

Industry observers note that surprisingly, some of these supposedly age-related markers were already present in young mouse hearts. Their presence suggests that the markers alone cannot reliably establish whether a cell has entered senescence, and that their meaning may depend on where they appear and the condition of the surrounding tissue.

"What surprised us was that some of these markers that have been associated with aging were already present in young hearts. They weren't where anyone expected to find them, and that forced us to rethink what those markers are telling us," Rosenthal said. "That turns the usual interpretation of cardiac aging on its ear because these markers alone don't mean a cell is senescent. There's nothing senescent about a six-month-old mouse heart.".

Sources indicate that the researchers also identified genes that became more active with age and were especially prominent in the same regions. Among them were Ccl8, which helps transmit inflammatory signals, and Cdkn1a (also known as p21), a gene widely used as an indicator of cellular senescence. Their locations provided further evidence that the valves and aortic root may be particularly vital areas for understanding how the heart ages.

In a recent development, "We're not talking about single genes. We're talking about an entire conversation between immune cells and fibroblasts. As the heart ages, the way those cells communicate changes, and that shift appears to be linked to the inflammation and tissue remodeling we see in older hearts," Rosenthal stated.

Male and Female Hearts Show Different Aging Patterns.

The study uncovered another crucial distinction: Aging did not produce exactly the same molecular changes in male and female mouse hearts.

Sources indicate that in males, aging fibroblasts showed stronger connections to biological processes associated with fibrosis. In females, the corresponding changes were more closely related to pathways involved in heart development and protein production.

It has been revealed that rosenthal noted that these differences may offer clues about cardiovascular aging in humans. Heart disease tends to become more common in women after menopause, while its development in men generally follows a more gradual pattern. The distinct cellular changes observed in male and female mice could help researchers investigate the biological processes behind these differences.

Sources indicate that however, the results describe differences in molecular activity, not demonstrated differences in heart function or disease risk. Further research will be needed to determine how these patterns influence cardiovascular health.

To explore whether their findings might also apply to people, the team compared the mouse results with previously published data from human hearts. Several molecular processes associated with aging, including pathways involved in responding to cellular stress, appeared in both species. This overlap suggests that at least some of the biological changes identified in mice may also be relevant to human heart aging.

"Our findings change the focus from aging across the entire heart to specific anatomical hotspots, helping us better understand how inflammation and fibrosis are connected and which regions of the heart are involved in the aging process," stated study author Amalia Sintou, a postdoctoral associate at JAX.

Could These Discoveries Help Protect Aging Hearts?

Although the research does not yet identify a latest treatment, it offers scientists a more detailed understanding of where aging-related changes occur and which cells are involved. By revealing these cellular patterns, the findings could help guide future studies aimed at reducing cardiovascular decline, maintaining healthy heart function, and improving health later in life.

Rosenthal's team is now examining whether exercise, diet, and disease alter the interactions between immune cells and connective tissue cells. The researchers hope to distinguish the normal effects of aging from changes that may leave the heart increasingly vulnerable to cardiovascular problems.

It has been revealed that the experimental design also helped the team isolate aging itself as a contributing factor. Because the mice lived under the same conditions and received the same diet, the researchers could investigate age-related changes without the additional variation introduced by different environments or eating habits.

"Valve replacement is common in older adults, and one of the significant questions is how much of the underlying damage is driven by aging itself," remarked study author Aleksandra Aljakna Khan, a postdoctoral associate at JAX. "Because all of the mice in our study lived in the same environment and ate the same diet, we were able to isolate the effects of aging and show that aging alone can initiate some of these changes in the valves and aorta.".

It has been revealed that together, the findings suggest that understanding heart aging requires looking beyond the muscle responsible for pumping blood. The valves, major blood vessels, and supporting cells may play a much larger role than previously recognized. Learning how these structures change and communicate over time could eventually help scientists identify ways to preserve cardiovascular health as people age.

Research Funding and Study Authors.

In a recent development, the research received funding from the NIH Common Fund through The Jackson Laboratory Senescence Tissue Mapping Center (JAX-Sen TMC U54 AG079753). Additional support came from JAX's National Cancer Institute-designated Cancer Center (P30 CA034196).

According to recent reports, additional authors from The Jackson Laboratory included Yue Zhao, Antonios Somarakis, Harshpreet Chandok, Juliana Alcoforado Diniz, Ramalakshmi Ramasamy, Gretchen T. Clark, Brian S. White, Paul Robson, Ron Korstanje, and J. Matthew Mahoney. Leon Frommer and Sikander Hayat of RWTH Aachen University also contributed to the study.

  • According to recent reports, as the name suggests, the Challenge Stradale is a road-going variant of the 296 that shares a lot in common with the race car at the moment used in various Ferrari Challenge series.
  • Those components combine to create a massive 1360 pounds of downforce at 155 miles per hour, an increase of 72 percent over the 296 GTB that won Road & Track Performance Car of the Year in 2024.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The upcoming-for-2026 Ferrari 296 Speciale is a sharper, faster, and more track-oriented variant of the brand’s V-6 supercar—but that doesn’t mean it is the only high-performance variant of the car that Ferrari will build. In a somewhat surprising break from recent tradition, Ferrari is also going to make a Challenge Stradale variant of the 296 to sell alongside the Speciale.

According to recent reports, as the name suggests, the Challenge Stradale is a road-going variant of the 296 that shares a lot in common with the race car at the moment used in various Ferrari Challenge series. Specifically, its aerodynamic elements are strikingly similar to the new 296 Challenge Evo, which was revealed alongside the new road car on November 21. The massive rear wing, front dive planes, and aggressive rear splitter are all extremely similar to design elements seen on that race car.

Those components combine to create a massive 1360 pounds of downforce at 155 miles per hour, an increase of 72 percent over the 296 GTB that won Road & Track Performance Car of the Year in 2024. Downforce is also up 401 lbs at that speed on the 296 Speciale, an increase of 29 percent.

According to recent reports, the removal of the hybrid system means a reduction in power, dropping from a combined system output of 819 horsepower in the 296 GTB to an engine-only output of 670 hp in the Challenge Stradale. The simplified powertrain and stripped out interior mean serious reductions in weight to match, though; the Challenge Stradale is 309 lbs lighter than the GTB and 176 lbs lighter than the Speciale.

Industry observers note that does the reduction in weight and increase in downforce make the 296 Challenge Stradale faster than the hybrid 296 Speciale already on the market? Not necessarily. Ferrari claims the Challenge Stradale is half a second a lap faster at its Fiorano test track, but marginally slower at a high-speed circuit like Monza. The more powerful Speciale should be quicker on other tracks with the on-throttle time necessary to allow the hybrid to stretch its legs, while the lighter Challenge Stradale should have the advantage on more technical circuits with more off-throttle time.

The other major differentiation between the Speciale and the Challenge Stradale is availability. While that other high-end 296 variant was a limited-run model, Ferrari stresses that the Challenge Stradale is a part of its regular lineup, and should be more available to buyers. It remains a Ferrari, so the market is unlikely to be flooded with 296s with massive wings in the years to come, but by supercar standards, it should be relatively attainable.

Recent findings suggest that ferrari has not yet unveiled a price for the American market, but the brand notes that it should start at the equivalent of just under $320,000 in Italy, including value-added tax. Prices in one region do not necessarily translate directly to another, but that number would leave the 296 Challenge Stradale in the general range of the similarly track-focused likes of Porsche’s 911 GT3 RS and Ford’s Mustang GTD.

Waymo Is Recalling Its Robotaxis Because They're Not Great At Dealing With Human Instructions

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (955 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Waymo recalled its robotaxis again on Friday, citing issues with navigating closed freeway lanes and handling manually controlled intersections.
  • The company's robotaxis were banned from California freeways earlier this month after a few high-profile incidents.
  • In a recent development, the robotaxis seem to be very adept at dealing with normal road conditions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Waymo recalled its robotaxis again on Friday, citing issues with navigating closed freeway lanes and handling manually controlled intersections. For anyone who has been following Waymo closely, this shouldn't be that surprising.

The company's robotaxis were banned from California freeways earlier this month after a few high-profile incidents. Waymo took the voluntary step of suspending interstate operation nationwide on Wednesday, meaning the entire fleet is now back to running primarily on local roads and minor state highways.

In a recent development, the robotaxis seem to be very adept at dealing with normal road conditions. But the trouble seems to be when something unexpected pops up. Regulators from California cited poor behavior surrounding closed lanes and construction zones, a recurring issue for the organization, along with a another recent high-profile incident involving a California Highway Patrol rolling road block.

In a recent development, if you don't know what that last sentence means, you aren't alone. When I first moved to California a few years ago, I had no idea what a rolling road block or "traffic break" meant in normal parlance. But drive California freeways long enough and you'll experience one. A CHP cruiser or a group of them joins the highway, puts on its lights, and slowly zigzags across all lanes of traffic, blocking drivers from passing or exceeding the speed of the maneuver. The goal is typically to create a safe break in traffic for authorities to removed debris, clear and accident, or otherwise operate on the road. Sometimes it just slows down the herd before it barrels into a blind-corner accident scene at 80 mph.

In a recent development, when I first experienced this, I was plenty confused. But when I saw cops swerving in front of me with lights on, I naturally just slowed down and stayed behind me. Common sense told me that a cop swerving around with their lights on probably isn't looking for a race. Unfortunately, though, autonomous driving software doesn't always know how to interpret novel situations. So when a Waymo got caught behind a rolling road block, here's what it did:.

Yep, it tried to blow right by. CHP was able to hold it back, but I've seen a Trooper controlling six lanes of traffic with one car before. Add in an inventive and disobedient robotaxi and you can see how it could create a dangerous situation wherein an autonomous vehicle is driving down a road that construction workers or police think is effectively closed.

Now, Waymos are good enough at avoiding hitting things that I don't expect this would have been too bad. But even a small chance of a runaway robotaxi is unacceptable to regulators and to Waymo, so it's good to pause freeway operations until they figure things out.

But the road block situation is indicative of a larger problem with autonomous vehicles, and perhaps the most interesting one. We think of driving as a predominantly legal or process-driven endeavor. You stop at stop signs, obey the speed limit, and keep it between the lines. Errors happen, but we tend to see them as based on improperly applied rules.

In a recent development, yet the police here are disrupting the rules and enforcing an unscheduled and ad-hoc temporary speed limit and traffic flow. If you're from out of state or haven't experienced it yet, it's confusing, as there's direct ruleset for an impromptu situation like that. Yet any other driver caught in this situation wouldn't blow past the cop car. Like me, they'd approach it cautiously, and let the police car take the lead.

Sources indicate that that is the issue I'm referring to: Driving is not just about rules and infrastructure. It's a social behavior. We wave each other ahead at stop signs and intersections. We signal our intent for an aggressive merge by riding the side of the lane market. You look at people's faces to gaze intention and attention. And when the traffic lights are down or the road is blocked by falling trees, we create impromptu order where chaos exists, nodding or waving to signal that it's someone else's term.

Industry observers note that this was always going to be the hard part for robotaxis. That's why the same recall applies to another troubled behavioral pattern for Waymos: They struggle when officers or city workers are manually controlling and intersection. Whether it's due to a high-traffic event or an outage, it's not all that uncommon to see a police officer directing traffic by hand. They wave you through or hold you back.

According to recent reports, but what happens if the car loses sight of the person directing traffic? What if the person directing traffic isn't actually a police officer, and waves you through a red light? What if the alternate route the police point you to spits the robotaxi onto a highway, where it isn't allowed to go?

According to recent reports, there are a million more what-ifs related to this social component of driving. All of them will have to be encountered and solved as they come, just as you and I eventually figured these things out. Recall by recall, we'll turn these Waymos into upstanding citizens.

#109510. Here are 7 great reasons rural drivers SHOULD embrace EVs in 2027

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1701 w)

Here are 7 great reasons rural drivers SHOULD embrace EVs in 2027

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1701 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, america’s heartland is full of rural communities that are miles away from its major cities, both geographically and culturally – but that doesn’t mean these more sparsely populated regions can’t reap the benefits of electrification.
  • UPGRADE 21NOV2026: this is an annual (ish) post I have been updating since 2024.
  • In a recent development, “An electric lifestyle would be a boon to our rural heartland,” wrote the Union of Concerned Scientists’ Maria Cecilia Pinto de Moura.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, america’s heartland is full of rural communities that are miles away from its major cities, both geographically and culturally – but that doesn’t mean these more sparsely populated regions can’t reap the benefits of electrification. In fact, EVs offer rural drivers even more benefits than they do to city-dwellers!

UPGRADE 21NOV2026: this is an annual (ish) post I have been updating since 2024.

In a recent development, “An electric lifestyle would be a boon to our rural heartland,” wrote the Union of Concerned Scientists’ Maria Cecilia Pinto de Moura. “Rural communities across the country have their own distinguishing characteristics, but certain shared characteristics such as driving distances, the type of vehicles driven, and socio-economics are factors which contribute to this larger potential to benefit from vehicle electrification.”.

Sources indicate that pinto de Moura went on to outline five ways rural and country drivers could benefit from going electric – but that was in 2021, and a whole lot has changed in the nearly six years since. As such, I thought it was high time we revisit some of the reasons EVs are a great fit for rural lifestyles, see if we could uncover any fresh ones, and outline the reasons we think rural drivers should rush to embrace electric vehicles in the coming calendar year.

When you hear that line about, “the average American drives 30 to 40 miles a day,” remember that in towns like Wellington, Ohio, or Colfax, Washington, 30 miles is a grocery run. Each way. So when people trot out that old line about range anxiety, what rural drivers actually hear isn’t reassurance. It’s dismissal — a suggestion that they drive too far for an EV to work, when nothing could be further from the truth.

A recent study by Rural Climate Partnership found that rural drivers spend an average of 44% more on fuel than city dwellers, and that the top 3.6% of rural drivers — the “supermilers” who rack up the most miles — could save over $4,000 each year by switching to electric fuel.

Country guys and gals love their pickups, and arguably the biggest difference between the EV market of 2021 and 2027 is that electric trucks and SUVs are no longer a novelty. There are now battery-powered options ready to haul, handle chores, head out camping, and tow a trailer.

What’s more, a new wave of more affordable electric trucks from Ford, Slate, and others is challenging the idea that you need a $50,000 half-ton pickup to get real work done. Early interest suggests there’s plenty of pent-up demand for capable, accessible electric work trucks that don’t need to be twenty feet long or cost more than what your parent’s paid for their house.

Industry observers note that with only about 45% of rural counties having access to DC fast charging, public charging still isn’t as visible as many first-time EV buyers might like, but it’s far better than it used to be — and improving fast. Still, that’s not the real EV advantage. Home charging is.

Unlike many apartment-dwelling urban drivers, most rural owners can charge right at home. More than 80% of rural households have a driveway or garage that are ideal for overnight Level 2 charging, and many already have a 240V outlet, keeping setup costs (if there even are any) to a minimum.

Plug in before bed, wake up to a full battery every morning, and do it for pennies on the dollar, especially with off-peak rates.

If disaster strikes and you lose power, your EV could be more than just a way to get around. Many electric cars and trucks have the ability to power refrigerators, freezers, well pumps, lights, and other household essentials for days, either through onboard outlets or a dedicated vehicle-to-home (V2H) system that feeds electricity directly into your home’s electrical panel. Ford’s from-the-ashes F-150 Lightning and Tesla’s Cybertruck are already among the EVs making that capability a reality, and newer, more affordable electric trucks promise to bring V2H tech to even more households.

If you live in an area prone to extreme weather, where severe storms, hurricanes, or wildfires can leave homes without electricity for days, that’s a pretty compelling benefit. Keeping food cold, medical equipment running or essential medication refrigerated can be a literal lifesaver – and your EV’s battery might be the biggest backup power source you own.

It’s been a few years since a working class guy could reasonably expect to get a new pickup for less than $50,000. And, while much has been made of the “high cost of electric vehicles,” the truth is that thanks to killer lease deals, new tax incentives, and companies like Ford Pro and TRC that are willing to help you find even more funding to help pay for them, EVs can often be had for less than a comparable gas model.

As such, getting behind the wheel of an ultra-powerful, ultra smooth-running electric pickup truck from your favorite brand is easier than ever.

Recent findings suggest that at the risk of sounding like a paranoid red hat, rural Americans are proud Americans – just like rural Canadians are proud Canadians. Unfortunately, every gallon of gas burned in their pickups and SUVs came from oil drilled, refined, and traded on global markets — and that means supporting the oil business and economies of nations whose values don’t always align with, or maybe are even outright hostile to theirs.

Switching to an EV can help more of that money right here at home, especially as more and better battery recycling efforts come online and newer battery and anode/cathode chemistries are developed, reducing dependence on rare Earth metals, cobalt, and even lithium.

Even better, thanks to the rapid expansion and dramatically reduced costs of wind and solar power, you can power your EV with energy that is 100% Made in the USA, that doesn’t support foreign oil interests or involve you in a bunch of dumb oil wars (except indirectly), and which creates good-paying construction and maintenance jobs for local workers.

In my experience, rural buyers appreciate things that last, and are moved more by lasting quality than fleeting fashions – and that’s exactly why they should be looking at EVs.

We recently covered a 2019 Chevy Bolt that had put more than 470,000 miles on its odometer, along with data from Ford showing its battery packs maintain more than 90% of their battery health after 100,000 miles.

And while we’re talking about data, it should be noted that EVs aren’t some fresh, unknown technology. The first modern high-voltage car battery hit the road more than 30 years ago (the Prius was released in 1996, as a 1997 model). Some of those cars are still on the road – and there are literally tens of thousands of EVs out there still performing their daily driver duties every day.

There are obviously more reasons to go electric than these, from lower cost of ownership to saving the planet to absolutely killer burnouts that would make the one-tire-fire era IROC Camaros hang their 305s in shame – but I think those kind of fade into the background as being appealing to just about everyone, instead of being especially appealing to rural drivers.

Recent findings suggest that I live in rural Australia in a village that doesn't even have a fuel bowser. My shopping trip is usually around 164km (100miles). I have solar on my roof. I now have an EV (one of the Chinese brands that aren't available in the USA) and am delighted with it. I'm saving a lot of money on fuel and because the solar feed-in tariff goes negative in the middle of the day (I have to pay the utility manufacturer to take my electricity) by charging the car at home I save money there. For rural people with roof space for solar EVs should be a no-brainer, but like many rural areas my district is incredibly conservative (do a search for Barnaby Joyce, my local member) and the populace are convinced they don't drive far enough, they'll catch on fire (mine has an LFP battery, so the risk is low) and that I'll need to replace the battery in a year (even though the battery has an 8 year warranty).

Recent findings suggest that that remarked, it’s been a long time since I was back in Ohio, so maybe I’ve forgotten what it’s like. You guys are smart, head on down to the comments and let me know what I missed!

Legendary game creator Vince Zampella has passed away

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died.
  • According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles.
  • Industry observers note that vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Industry observers note that vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

According to recent reports, zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Recent findings suggest that zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

According to recent reports, respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA noted in a statement.

Sources indicate that “While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he indicated up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”.

#109508. Tech Report: Vitamin B12 may hold the key to treating a rare genetic disorder

Tech Report: Vitamin B12 may hold the key to treating a rare genetic disorder

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (681 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A surprising discovery involving vitamin B12 could open new possibilities for understanding and potentially treating rare genetic disorders.
  • According to recent reports, the findings center on a cellular process called RNA splicing, which helps prepare the genetic instructions cells use to produce proteins.
  • In a recent development, mutations in genes responsible for splicing can cause conditions such as Verheij syndrome.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A surprising discovery involving vitamin B12 could open new possibilities for understanding and potentially treating rare genetic disorders. Researchers found that the vitamin can correct developmental problems in tiny worms carrying a genetic mutation associated with Verheij syndrome, a rare human condition that causes developmental delays, impaired growth, and short stature.

According to recent reports, the findings center on a cellular process called RNA splicing, which helps prepare the genetic instructions cells use to produce proteins. During splicing, unnecessary portions of messenger RNA are removed, and the remaining sections are joined together in the correct order. When this process goes wrong, it can disrupt essential cellular functions and contribute to serious developmental disorders.

In a recent development, mutations in genes responsible for splicing can cause conditions such as Verheij syndrome. To better understand the effects of these genetic changes, scientists investigated how a related mutation affects growth and metabolism in a laboratory model.

Vitamin B12 Reverses Developmental Defects in Worms.

Industry observers note that the discovery emerged from experiments involving C. elegans, a tiny roundworm commonly used in biological research. The researchers were initially searching for previously unknown genes that influence lifespan when they began examining a mutation in a gene involved in RNA splicing. The same gene is associated with Verheij syndrome in humans.

Worms carrying the mutation developed problems resembling notable features of the human disorder. Their growth slowed considerably, and they remained smaller than normal.

To investigate why this happened, the scientists conducted genetic screens and analyzed the worms' metabolism. They discovered that the mutation disrupted specific metabolic pathways that depend on vitamin B12 and are essential for healthy growth and normal cellular activity.

The researchers then tested whether providing additional vitamin B12 could counteract these changes. Remarkably, the treatment restored the affected metabolic processes to normal and corrected the developmental abnormalities associated with the mutation.

Sources indicate that "We were surprised to find that a change in a fundamental process of RNA processing had such a targeted effect on vitamin B12-dependent metabolism," indicates Jonathan Kölschbach, first author of the study. "Even more exciting was that we were able to largely correct the consequences of this change in the worm model using vitamin B12.".

Could Vitamin B12 Help Treat a Rare Genetic Disorder?

It has been revealed that to explore whether their findings might also apply to people, the researchers examined publicly available datasets from human cells. They also worked with Hormos Dafsari, a neuropediatrician at the University Hospital Cologne, to collect blood samples from patients diagnosed with Verheij syndrome.

These investigations uncovered evidence of similar metabolic changes in humans, suggesting that the vitamin B12-related pathways affected in the worms may also play a role in the human disorder.

In a recent development, although the results are promising, researchers have not yet established whether vitamin B12 supplementation can improve symptoms in people with Verheij syndrome. Additional studies will be necessary to determine whether the benefits observed in worms can be translated into a treatment for patients.

The discovery also raises a broader possibility. Metabolic disruptions may contribute more substantially to diseases caused by faulty RNA splicing than scientists previously recognized. Understanding these connections could help researchers identify new therapeutic strategies, potentially extending beyond Verheij syndrome to other rare genetic conditions.

"Our study is a good example of how basic research on model organisms can provide upcoming insights into human diseases," claims Adam Antebi, Director at the Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing and lead author of the study. "A fundamental biological question can thus give rise to a new approach that could also become medically relevant in the long term.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a red wave of Chinese-built electric vehicles breaks over Europe and Canada, Xiaomi is selling its electric cars outside of China for the first time ever – and its starting its push for global growth with the UAE in 2027.

Xiaomi is selling its electrified vehicles to buyers outside of China for first time this week, with the SU7 sedan, YU7 crossover, and Skynomad SUV now listed for sale throughout the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The tech giant isn’t going it alone, however.

Xiomi is working local distributor Gargash Prime Automotive, rather than operating its own retail network, with Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun confirming that the tech giant would officially enter Western car markets next year at the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen held 17NOV.

CarNewsChina reports that Gargash Prime Automotive is offering 13 variants across the Xiaomi SU7 sedan, YU7 SUV, and Skynomad extended-range electric SUV lineup, with retail prices starting at 169,900 AED ($~46,200 US) for the SU7 Standard and climbing all the way up to 375,900 AED ($~102,000 US) for the range-topping SU7 Ultra.

Not to lump a bunch of nations with their own rich heritage and car culture together, but it’s fair to say that drivers in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Kuwait love their supercars – and the brand’s Xiaomi SU7 Ultra might be one of the most super of them all, thanks to fully 1,548 hp from three high-torque electric motors, the SU7 Ultra can sprint from 0-100 km/h (62 mph) in under two seconds on its way to a towering, 217 mph top speed.

It’s not just a straight-line speed machine, either. Xiaomi gave its go-fast flagship a serious track-focused makeover on its way to becomig the “Utlra,” complete with carbon-ceramic brakes, an aggressive (if controversial) composite aero package, an enormous rear wing, and a chassis tuned to tackle the turns the Green Hell of the Nürburgring.

And, at a relatively reasonable $102,000 equivalent price, I’d be willing to bet that a lot of the hypercar-loving Emiratis will be eager to get their hands on one.

The first customer deliveries of the Xiaomi SU7 Standard and Ultra, YU7 Standard, and Skynomad N70 Pro models are scheduled for December of this year, with deliveries of the remaining variants scheduled for February 2027.

Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them?
  • The technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results.
  • It has been revealed that quantum systems are expected to become capable of solving increasingly complex problems that traditional computers struggle with or cannot handle at all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them? Scientists have now developed a promising latest method that could help overcome this challenge by measuring the accuracy of quantum simulations and identifying how much uncertainty their predictions contain.

The technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results. Researchers successfully demonstrated the approach using a quantum simulator with up to 51 qubits in Innsbruck, Austria.

It has been revealed that quantum systems are expected to become capable of solving increasingly complex problems that traditional computers struggle with or cannot handle at all. However, this progress creates a verification problem. When a simulation is small enough, scientists can compare its results with calculations performed on a conventional computer. As quantum systems grow beyond those limits, that direct comparison becomes impractical, making alternative ways to assess their reliability essential.

A New Way to Measure Quantum Computing Accuracy.

It has been revealed that the breakthrough comes from an international research team led by Tristan Kraft at the Technical University of Munich and Peter Zoller at the University of Innsbruck and the Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information of the Austrian Academy of Sciences, working alongside Barbara Kraus of the Technical University of Munich. The researchers developed a method for experimentally determining how a quantum simulator operates and translating uncertainties in its behavior into measurable limits on the accuracy of its results.

According to recent reports, quantum simulators are specialized physical systems designed to reproduce the behavior of other quantum systems. They are especially useful for investigating situations involving large numbers of interacting particles, where the calculations required can promptly overwhelm even powerful conventional computers.

But quantum experiments are never entirely free from errors. "But no real experiment is perfect," says Tristan Kraft. "Interactions may turn out differently than expected, the system is influenced by its environment, and measurements are also subject to uncertainties.".

In a recent development, rather than assuming a quantum simulator behaves exactly as intended, the latest approach examines experimental data to determine what is actually happening inside the system. This allows researchers to identify crucial interactions and account for disturbances such as fluctuations and noise.

"From this data, we determine the relevant interactions as well as key influences from fluctuations and noise. We then calculate how the uncertainties in this model affect the simulation results," explains Tristan Kraft. "The quantum simulator thus provides not just a single value, but a result with error margins that quantify its accuracy.".

Successfully Tested on a 51 Qubit Quantum Simulator.

To evaluate the method, the researchers began with a relatively small quantum system containing ten trapped ions. Because conventional computers can still calculate the behavior of a system of this size, the team could test its reconstructed models and calculated error limits against independent measurements.

After this initial validation, the researchers expanded their experiments to a chain of 51 trapped ions. The larger demonstration, carried out by a team led by Manoj Joshi and Christian Roos using an ion trap quantum simulator, highlighted that the technique could also work with substantially more complex quantum systems.

This represents an important step toward establishing how trustworthy quantum simulation results are, particularly as quantum devices advance into territory where direct verification with traditional computing methods becomes increasingly difficult.

Extending the Breakthrough to More Complex Quantum Systems.

Sources indicate that the next challenge is to bring the technique to two-dimensional quantum simulators. These systems can model more complicated interactions among particles, making them valuable for exploring quantum physics. At the same time, their growing complexity makes their results particularly difficult to confirm using conventional calculations.

Sources indicate that "This is particularly vital because classical calculations for such systems become significantly more difficult as the number of particles increases," explains quantum computing pioneer Peter Zoller. "This also makes independent verification of the results increasingly complex, making the question of experimentally determined error limits all the more important.".

The researchers are now adapting their method for the newest generation of two-dimensional quantum simulators, which offer improved precision and can investigate systems containing larger numbers of particles.

Industry observers note that looking further ahead, the approach could help scientists establish a more meaningful way to measure quantum advantage, the ability of quantum systems to outperform conventional computers. Instead of comparing machines based only on their processing speed or the size of the problems they can handle, researchers could also examine how accurately each system produces its answers.

Industry observers note that "After all, when a classical computer and a quantum simulator tackle the same problem, it's not just a matter of which one delivers a result faster. What's also crucial is which one can solve the problem with a smaller, verifiable margin of error," indicates Peter Zoller.

Sources indicate that this shift could change how progress in quantum computing is evaluated. Future breakthroughs may be judged not simply by how many particles a simulator can model or how swiftly it performs calculations, but by its ability to solve increasingly difficult problems with demonstrably reliable results.

The findings were published in Physical Review X. The research received support from the Austrian Science Fund (FWF), the German Ministry of Research, Technology and Space, the European Union, BMW, and other funding organizations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Max Verstappen started on pole for the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday evening and held the lead at one point on every lap, but the race was far more thrilling than that would let on.

Verstappen qualified second and inherited pole after pole-sitter Kimi Antonelli received a five-place grid penalty.

At the start, Max Verstappen took the lead from George Russell and kept his elbows out as he had the hardest spot on the track, punching through the crisp air with no help from a slipstream.

Sources indicate that on the second lap of the race, Russell, in a much faster Mercedes, passed Verstappen in the final corners coming off the Las Vegas Strip straight, then lost the lead before the first corner of the next lap. He would repeat this multiple times throughout the first half of the Grand Prix.

The race recorded a record 35 lead changes, but no one could cement a run past Verstappen.

With Verstappen slowing the field behind him, the first 10 laps of the race found the top three within one second and the top ten within less than 4.5 seconds.

On lap 20, Sergio Perez tried to make a pick on Rafeal Camera and the Haas, and Cadillac ended up tangled in the barrier, bringing out a full safety car. In a normal race, this would’ve neutralized the race, but with everyone still running bunched up, it just sent the field all together to the pits, leading to teams double-stacking against each other.

Hamilton was the biggest loser at the pit stop, having to serve a 10-second penalty that was not yet shared with him for a battle with Norris that he thought was just.

Hamilton was kept out while everyone else pitted to clear space for Charles Leclerc and was told about his penalty.

“Ah, that’s shit. If I turned in, we would’ve crashed.”.

It has been revealed that under the safety car, Arvid Lindblad spun on cold tires to end his campaign for his first-ever podium. Arvid had his best starting spot of fifth for the Grand Prix and ran as high as third, while the Red Bulls on his sister team ran 1-2; he fell out of the points with the mistake.

It has been revealed that shortly after racing resumed, Isack Hadjar, who challenged his teammate Verstappen for the lead in the first half of the race and often put in the hardest position between the leader and the charging field, hit debris on the track and damaged his front wing. Hadjar pitted and finished outside the points as well.

With Red Bull and VCARB drivers out of contention, the door reopened for the Mercedes as Kimi Antonelli made his way into the picture following his grid drop, and Russell never left.

With two laps to go, Antonelli led Russell as the teammate fought for second; in turn 5, Russell went for the pass, overcommitted, and slid into the barrier.

Verstappen laughed on from ahead following a weekend of tension between the front-row starters.

Antonelli fell away from the lead battle on the penultimate lap with an internal glitch and would come home fourth.

Industry observers note that in the mayhem, the McLarens saw their luck change at Las Vegas. Following this double disqualification while battling for the championship last year, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri walked away with a shocking first double podium of the season.

“I led for about 15 seconds, so I’m very proud,” Norris joked.

Antonelli was followed by Pierre Gasly, Franco Colapinto, Lewis Hamilton, Carlos Sainz, George Russell and Charles Leclerc in the points-paying positions.

Her daily driver is a 2010 Subaru that she refused to do the smallest amount of preventative maintenance on. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you can believe it, Love and Deepspace is almost two-years-old, and Infold Games is celebrating the moment in a few major ways. The Throne of Eros update brings the game up to version 5.0, and it’s one for fans of all love interests.

For one, this is the first time all five of them are brought together. The update is also adding some key fresh features, alongside anniversary events, and more.

In a recent development, throne of Eros also doubles as the latest Wish Pool, which is the one that has all of the game’s love interests in a single banner. This is a limited-time affair, of course, but it’s not the only thing you should look forward to here.

There’s also the Memory Growth Bonus, another limited-time event that you can take advantage of to grow your Memories. The even bigger news is that you can target your Wishes through the Xspace Echo, which lets you select five Memories to create your own pool from. You can use this to get any Memories you might not have, of course.

On the topic of Memories, you’ll also be able to unlock upcoming second anniversary KV Memories, as part of a Yearly Highlights Event that will let you look back on your own journey with the game over the past year.

In a recent development, on the story and narrative side, Throne of Eros adds two fresh main stories, with new branches for Xavier, and Rafayel. There’s even a narrative-specific event that will run throughout the anniversary period, through which you can earn two daily outfits for each of the five love interests.

The celebrations also extend to newly introduced anniversary content like mail, and video calls. You can purchase a Yearly Pass, and check out some new arrivals at the Lunar Shop.

Beyond the anniversary content, version 5.0 also adds a latest feature to the game: Home, which essentially offers a hub to get you directly to interacting with love interests that doesn’t have to do with combat or story.

You can also expect various other quality of life updates that touch on the Journal, Phone Moments Search, Resources Quick Cleanup, and new Tete-a-Tete that should make interacting with all of them more streamlined.

While this is a special banner, you should brush up on how banners work in Love and Deepspace if you’re unfamiliar. As always, it’s never not a good idea to check our Love and Deepspace codes page for some freebies.

Industry News: Tesla FSD V15 Makes Your Drive Look Like Grand Theft Auto

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla’s latest version of Full Self-Driving lets you swing a virtual camera around your car like you’re cruising through Leonida in Grand Theft Auto.
  • The feature is called Tesla Reality View, and it’s reaching early-access users with FSD V15.
  • Tesla’s biggest FSD V15 claim takes a little unpacking.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla’s latest version of Full Self-Driving lets you swing a virtual camera around your car like you’re cruising through Leonida in Grand Theft Auto. It’s a neat trick, especially when you consider that the Tesla has to generate the scenery as it goes. It also gets a little floating arrow, which now lets you know which roundabout exit it’s going to take.

The feature is called Tesla Reality View, and it’s reaching early-access users with FSD V15. The earlier parking display drew outlines of nearby objects, but this one recreates the street around you in real time and indicates where FSD intends to turn or park. You can have this on the whole screen, split it with the map, or let the map take over instead. There’s also a quieter cabin mode, and even the turn signal now fades sound after a few clicks.

Tesla’s biggest FSD V15 claim takes a little unpacking. The manufacturer says it's now 25 times safer when it does critical interventions. The upgrade to the software that interprets camera images was trained on millions of internet videos and shared with its Robotaxi and Optimus programs.

Industry observers note that what’s not clear is the starting figure. How many miles did the previous version go between critical interventions, and under what conditions? Tesla doesn’t say.

Sources indicate that will drivers actually notice? Tesla indicates V15 is better at spotting potholes, small animals, signs, and debris, including chains (which have been known to cause crashes drawing federal scrutiny). It should also avoid deep standing water and choose more appropriate speeds in school zones and bad weather.

Tesla says the navigation now learns from the routes other Teslas actually take, initially at the start and end of a trip. Tesla plans to extend that approach to the whole route later. Once you arrive, the map can show several parking options, and FSD uses your parking history to help pick one. It’s another application of the fleet learning feature Tesla demonstrated with V12.

V15 can also slow for a speed camera, but if you override it twice for the same camera, the car will remember your preference. Bike Rack Mode lets FSD operate with a rack on the tow hitch, though it won’t automatically reverse for you at the destination, leaving parking up to you. Autopark, Summon and backup warnings are disabled in that mode.

Industry observers note that in a roughly 25-minute drive, Sawyer Merritt found V15 more cautious around pedestrians than V14. In one parking lot, he mentioned the car braked for someone running across its path before he spotted them himself.

Recent findings suggest that while parking, Merritt could see which space FSD had picked, but tapping another space did nothing. He had to switch to manual, select the spot, and reengage FSD. It then parked where he wanted. That parking maneuver makes a pretty good case for the GTA graphics, which now give you a much better idea of what’s around the car and what it’s about to do, but the 25-fold safety improvement claim will need more than a drive to Best Buy to judge.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the last time Hyundai revealed a upcoming work truck was 22 years ago, and the Hyundai Porter has proven itself as a dependable workhorse throughout Korea and Southeast Asia – but only the pyramids and the Chevy Express can last forever. Hyundai is reportedly getting ready to pull the wraps off an all-new Porter pickup. This time, it’s electric.

Distinct from the Piaggio-branded Porter pickup that’s already sold in Europe, the Hyundai Porter is a conceptually similar, work-focused vehicle with a dropside pickup “bed” trailing a box-like passenger cab and a serious, professional-grade payload capacity.

In a recent development, carscoops recently published photos of a heavily camouflaged Hyundai Porter prototype last month, along with claims that Hyundai means to follow up the success of sister brand Kia’s multifunctional PV5 electric vans with a globally available electric version of the truck as early as next year. This week, the wraps came off, giving us our best look yet at what the truck might look like when it makes its official debut.

After feeding as many spy shots as I could into some AI models, we ended up with the images you see here. If they’re accurate, they show a commercial-ready EV that’s meant to attract new fleet buyers looking to ditch diesel in Western markets while serving as a direct, 1:1 replacement for domestic fleet operators already putting Porter pickups to work.

Industry observers note that those operators will probably feel a little safer behind the wheel of the latest truck, too. Hyundai has worked a short hood and crash structure into the bodywork where a conventional “flat” cabover now sits – a move that seems to point both to a commitment to provide better front-end protection to the truck’s occupants and an intent to at least take an honest run at the Euro NCAP crash standards.

Industry observers note that beyond that, we don’t really know anything about the upcoming Korean pickup – but it’s a safe bet that the next-generation Porter will benefit from some of the technology that’s been baked into the Hyundai Motor Group’s E-GMP.S commercial vehicle platform that underpins the Kia PV vehicles. Those ship with 51.5 and 71.2 kWh battery options sending electrons to 120 kW (~160 hp) electric motors, and while that’s far from a guarantee, it’s not nothing, either.

That’s my take, anyway – what’s yours? Will the Hyundai Porter EV make its way to the West on an AWD version of the E-GMP.S platform, or will it remain a regional model running on one of the organization’s hybrid platforms? Let us know in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4.
  • Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three upcoming playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.
  • The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of new content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three upcoming playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

It has been revealed that the Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

According to recent reports, speaking of elemental reactions, upcoming in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.
