New wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1035 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A latest wearable patch could offer a surprisingly simple way to improve one of the most important stages of sleep, without relying on medication or surgery.
  • Known as NEUSLeeP, the soft patch attaches to the skin and combines ultrasound stimulation with electrodes that monitor brain activity in real time.
  • REM sleep, short for rapid eye movement sleep, is the stage when most vivid dreaming occurs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A latest wearable patch could offer a surprisingly simple way to improve one of the most important stages of sleep, without relying on medication or surgery. Developed by researchers led by the University of Texas at Austin, the device uses gentle ultrasound waves to stimulate regions deep inside the brain, helping people enter REM sleep sooner and spend more time in this restorative stage.

Known as NEUSLeeP, the soft patch attaches to the skin and combines ultrasound stimulation with electrodes that monitor brain activity in real time. This allows researchers to influence brain regions involved in sleep while simultaneously tracking how the brain responds.

REM sleep, short for rapid eye movement sleep, is the stage when most vivid dreaming occurs. It also plays an vital role in processing emotions, consolidating memories, and adapting to stress. Disturbances in this stage of sleep have been associated with several mental health conditions, making it an important target for new treatments.

"This is the first time we've been able to noninvasively target deep brain regions involved in REM sleep, while simultaneously monitoring brain activity," said Kai Wing "Kevin" Tang, a recent UT biomedical engineering Ph.D. graduate who led the research effort.

Industry observers note that "Our skin-attached NEUSLeeP patch opens up new possibilities for understanding sleep and treating sleep disorders in home settings," added Huiliang "Evan" Wang, assistant professor in the Cockrell School of Engineering's Department of Biomedical Engineering. Wang supervised Tang's research and served as the principal investigator (PI) overseeing the project.

Sleep Patch Helps People Reach REM Sleep 43 Minutes Faster.

The early results suggest that the technology can make a measurable difference in how people experience REM sleep.

In a study involving 28 participants, published in Nature Communications, people using the patch entered REM sleep an average of 43 minutes sooner and spent approximately 16 additional minutes in that stage.

It has been revealed that these improvements were observed in both healthy sleepers and participants experiencing certain sleep difficulties. The volunteers also reported that the patch was comfortable to wear, with minimal adverse effects.

Unlike medications that affect the body more broadly, NEUSLeeP is designed to deliver stimulation to specific brain regions involved in sleep regulation. It uses ultrasound, a form of sound energy with frequencies beyond human hearing, to reach areas beneath the surface of the brain without requiring an invasive procedure.

The findings are encouraging, although the relatively small study means that larger trials will be needed to determine how consistently the technology works and whether its benefits persist over time.

Potential Benefits for Stress and Emotional Health.

The researchers also found evidence that the patch's effects may extend beyond increasing REM sleep.

Sources indicate that among healthy participants, ultrasound stimulation improved heart rate variability, a measure of the natural differences in time between consecutive heartbeats. This measurement provides insight into how the body's nervous system responds to stress and adjusts to changing conditions.

In a recent development, brain imaging revealed changes in neural circuits involved in emotional processing. Together, these findings suggest that improving REM sleep through targeted stimulation could potentially support emotional regulation and the ability to cope with stress.

"REM sleep is not just about dreaming -- it's about emotional reset and stress adaptation," explained Gregory Fonzo, assistant professor in the Dell Medical School's Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences and one of the project's co-PIs. "By enhancing REM, we may help people better cope with stress and improve their overall well-being.".

These possibilities are especially interesting because REM sleep disturbances have been linked to depression, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

According to recent reports, current approaches to sleep problems often involve medication or behavioral therapy. Although these treatments can be effective, medications may produce unwanted side effects, and existing approaches do not always directly address the biological processes responsible for disrupted REM sleep.

A device capable of influencing those processes without drugs or surgery could therefore offer an additional treatment option. However, the researchers have not yet established whether NEUSLeeP can improve symptoms of mental health disorders.

A Latest Direction for Treating Insomnia and PTSD.

Building on the initial findings, the research team looks to conduct larger clinical trials to confirm the patch's effects and investigate its potential use in people with PTSD, depression, and chronic insomnia.

Industry observers note that beyond treating sleep disorders, the technology could eventually support sleep monitoring at home and provide scientists with a newly introduced way to study how deep brain regions influence sleep. Researchers also envision personalized therapies that could be adjusted to individual sleep patterns and needs.

"Our vision is a future where patients with mental health disorders can optimize their sleep with a noninvasive and safe treatment," said Vincent Mysliwiec, M.D., a professor at UT Health San Antonio, a leading expert in sleep disorders, and another co-PI on the project. "This technology could help millions of people get the restorative sleep they need.".

The team is already taking steps toward making NEUSLeeP available beyond the research setting. Working with the university's commercialization unit, Discovery to Impact, the researchers are exploring how to bring the device to market and have filed a patent application covering the technology.

If future studies confirm the early results, this wearable ultrasound patch could become a valuable latest tool for improving REM sleep and potentially addressing conditions associated with poor sleep.

According to recent reports, other members of the research team include William D. Moscoso-Barrera, Mengxia Yu, Mengmeng Yao, Jinmo Jeong, Ilya Pyatnitskiy, Anakaren Romero Lozano, Jiachen Wang, Ju-Chun Hsieh, Tony Sungjin Chae, Daniel Song, Julieta Garcia, Rithvik Mittapalli, and Adam Bush of the Department of Biomedical Engineering; Benjamin Baird of the College of Natural Sciences' Department of Psychology; and Wynn Legon of Virginia Tech's Fralin Biomedical Research Institute.

Some mid-cycle updates focus on aesthetics, bringing some new style (and hopefully some new eyes) to a slightly older product. The 2027 Toyota Sienna skipped those pleasantries and focused on the meat and potatoes: its hybrid powertrain.

According to recent reports, the 2027 Toyota Sienna looks no different—unless you count the Cypress paint color, which was dropped and swapped with Storm Cloud—but it’s what’s lying under the body that matters more here. The Sienna adopts Toyota’s sixth-generation hybrid powertrain, which first arrived in the upscale Lexus ES Hybrid. A fresh electric motor packs more efficient silicon-carbide conductors, and it pairs with a 1.15-kWh battery that ditches the old nickel-metal hydride chemistry in favor of lithium-ion. In addition, there’s a whole new electrical platform underpinning it all, with new ECUs and software to manage everything.

See all results for fresh 2027 Toyota Sienna for sale near 03602.

Sources indicate that combine all that with a 2.5-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine that has been retuned for quieter low-speed operation, and you have a Toyota Sienna that produces a whopping six horsepower more than before, rising from 245 horses to 251. Engine torque is unchanged at 176 pound-feet, and Toyota did not specify e-motor torque. That small power bump is enough to affect its acceleration: Toyota estimates a 7.5-second sprint to 60 mph in front-wheel-drive Sienna variants, rising to 7.6 seconds with AWD. That’s 0.3 or 0.4 second quicker than before, respectively.

It has been revealed that even with that bump in speed, Toyota claims improved fuel economy in the 2027 Sienna, to the tune of +3 mpg in the city for FWD models and +4 mpg in the city for AWD models. Combined estimates rise 1 or 2 mpg. For context, the 2026 model is EPA estimated at 36 mpg city/36 highway/36 combined for the front-driver, and 35/36/35 for the AWD.

There have also been some tweaks to other electrical-adjacent components. The electronic power steering promises less effort at low speeds, while improving on-center feel at highway speeds. That adjustment includes a new steering-wheel layout that will eventually migrate to other sixth-gen-equipped hybrids. Toyota also fiddled with its brake electronics, resulting in less pedal effort and a smoother blend between regen and friction braking. The Sienna also includes something Toyota calls Vehicle Braking Posture Control, which applies braking to individual wheels with the aim to reduce body roll during cornering.

In a recent development, creature comforts get some upgrades as well. A 12.3-inch infotainment screen is now standard across the lineup (the LE grade ditches its 8.0-incher), as is a 12.3-inch gauge cluster (LE and XLE get this instead of the old 7.0-inch getup). There’s new LED cabin lighting, plus a revised rear-seat entertainment system that now features native apps on a new touchscreen. Upgraded dashboard sound abatement promises to lower the cabin volume by one decibel.

See all results for new 2027 Toyota Sienna for sale near 03602.

Toyota also slimmed down the Sienna’s trims for 2027. The Limited grade has been dropped in favor of adding more features to the sporty XSE variant, which rises to become the trim underneath the Platinum. As a result, the 2027 Sienna XSE picks up niceties like ventilated front seats with memory, a panoramic-view monitor, and a head-up display. The rugged Woodland Edition trim also picks up the surround-view tech. The upgraded rear-seat entertainment is available on the Woodland, XSE, and Platinum trims.

Sources indicate that the 2027 Toyota Sienna reaches dealerships in early—you guessed it—2027. Pricing starts around $44,500 for the front-wheel-drive LE base trim, which represents a price bump of less than $2000 over a base 2026 Sienna. Not too shabby for a whole fresh generation of powertrain.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 had a stellar launch, with two million XBOX players swarming to Latest Zealand to start their playthrough as early as possible, boasting eye-watering sales figures, and breaking viewership records.

Sources indicate that bugs and glitches are just a part of modern gaming. Some can be game-breaking, others produce some funny moments, and some can actually be useful. One GTA 6 glitch that is gathering a lot of attention is one that lets players access a first-person mode.

As expected, GTA 6 is played in third-person and although many players appreciate a first-person mode, it is absent at launch, or at least, officially.

There is a glitch that enables a first-person look. It can be a little fiddly at first, but once you get the hang of it, you will have a better view at the sights. We have all the details you need to know about how to enter first-person mode the next time you load up the game.

YouTuber OneBoyler posted a video demonstrating how to do the GTA 6 first-person glitch on PlayStation. To perform the glitch, pause the game and go to the in-game settings, under the Controller tab, scroll down until you see Touch Pad Button. Change the Touch Pad Button to Camera 2. This setting changes your touchpad from opening the map to altering your camera view.

Next, sit in the driver’s seat of a vehicle and take out your mobile phone by pressing up on the D-Pad. Put your phone away by hitting circle on a PlayStation controller and then instantly spam your touchpad button.

Recent findings suggest that once successful, you will see the world from your character’s perspective, holding the wheel of the car. From this point onward, you can safely exit the car with first-person view intact and even access your loadout. Equipping a gun allows you to hold it realistically, and the animations are compatible with first-person mode.

Sources indicate that bugs and glitches are just a part of modern gaming. Some can be game-breaking, others produce some funny moments, and some can actually be useful.

Sources indicate that also, you can drive in first-person, bringing a new level of immersion to the already gorgeous and detailed world around you. The city lights reflecting off the front of your car hit different when you’re cruising around the streets.

It’s worth noting that to return to third-person mode, you must reload your save. Make sure you save at the right time and don’t make any progress you want to risk losing while experimenting with the first-person view.

When GTA 5 debuted on XBOX 360 and PlayStation 3 back in 2013, a first-person mode was absent. Only when GTA 5 was ported to XBOX One, PlayStation 4, and PC did a first-person perspective arrive in the game. Included were an optional first-person cover system, a fresh targeting system, traditional FPS controls, and fresh animations that allowed players to see the world in a whole new way.

If history were to repeat itself, a first-person mode could be on the cards for GTA 6 in a future enhancement. For now, if you want to explore Leonida in first-person, you’ll have to do so using the glitch.

It’s unknown what the first post-launch GTA 6 patch will entail, but if it doesn’t bring a first-person mode with it, players will be hoping that Rockstar Games decides against patching out this particular bug.

#109494. Tech Report: Wine, beer, or spirits? Massive study reveals a surprising health divide

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1505 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Wine, beer, or spirits? Massive study reveals a surprising health divide

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1505 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A massive study involving more than 340,000 adults has uncovered a surprising difference in the health risks associated with wine, beer, cider, and spirits.
  • Researchers found that low to moderate wine consumption was associated with a lower risk of death, particularly from cardiovascular disease.
  • Industry observers note that the results also reinforce a broader conclusion from previous research: drinking less alcohol is generally better for health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A massive study involving more than 340,000 adults has uncovered a surprising difference in the health risks associated with wine, beer, cider, and spirits. Although heavy drinking was linked to worse health outcomes regardless of the beverage, the picture was more complicated among people who consumed smaller amounts of alcohol.

Researchers found that low to moderate wine consumption was associated with a lower risk of death, particularly from cardiovascular disease. In contrast, similar amounts of beer, cider, and spirits were linked to a higher risk. The findings, presented at the American College of Cardiology's Annual Scientific Session (ACC.26), suggest that both the type and quantity of alcohol may influence its relationship with long-term health.

Industry observers note that the results also reinforce a broader conclusion from previous research: drinking less alcohol is generally better for health. Importantly, the new findings do not establish that wine itself protects against disease.

"These results come from the general population, and in certain high-risk groups, such as people with chronic diseases or cardiovascular conditions, the risks could be even higher," remarked Zhangling Chen, MD, PhD, a professor at the Second Xiangya Hospital, Central South University in China and the study's senior author.

How a Study of 340,000 Adults Measured Alcohol Risk.

It has been revealed that to investigate the relationship between drinking habits and longevity, scientists examined data from 340,924 adults enrolled in the UK Biobank between 2006 and 2022. The UK Biobank is a large research resource that collects health and lifestyle information to help scientists investigate factors associated with disease and mortality.

Recent findings suggest that participants reported their alcohol consumption through dietary questionnaires when they joined the study. Researchers then classified them into four groups based on how much pure alcohol they typically consumed each day or week, rather than simply counting drinks.

It has been revealed that this distinction matters because beer, wine, and spirits contain different concentrations of alcohol. For comparison, a 12-ounce can of beer, a 5-ounce glass of wine, and a 1.5-ounce shot of spirits each provide approximately 14 grams of pure alcohol.

In a recent development, people consuming fewer than 20 g (about 1.5 standard drinks) per week were placed in the never or occasional drinking group. Low consumption was defined as 20 g per week up to 20 g per day for men, and 20 g per week up to 10 g per day for women.

Moderate drinking was defined as 20 g to 40 g (about 1.5 to three standard drinks) daily for men and 10 g to 20 g daily for women. High consumption meant more than 40 g (about three drinks) per day for men or more than 20 g (about 1.5 drinks) per day for women.

Researchers followed participants' health outcomes for an average of more than 13 years, allowing them to examine how drinking patterns were associated with deaths from different causes.

Wine, Beer, and Spirits Show Different Heart Health Risks.

Recent findings suggest that the clearest finding concerned heavy alcohol consumption. Compared with people who never drank or consumed alcohol only occasionally, heavy drinkers had a 24% higher risk of dying from any cause. Their risk of dying from cancer was 36% higher, while their risk of dying from heart disease was 14% higher.

These increased risks were associated with heavy drinking regardless of whether participants preferred wine, beer, cider, or spirits.

In a recent development, however, the results became more surprising when researchers examined low and moderate alcohol consumption. At these levels, the type of beverage was associated with substantially different outcomes.

People who consumed wine in low to moderate amounts had a significantly lower risk of death, while those who consumed comparable amounts of beer, cider, or spirits had a significantly higher risk.

Sources indicate that the contrast was especially striking for cardiovascular disease, a broad category of conditions affecting the heart and blood vessels. Moderate wine drinkers had a 21% lower risk of dying from cardiovascular disease than people who never or only occasionally drank alcohol.

By comparison, even low consumption of beer, cider, or spirits was associated with a 9% higher risk of cardiovascular death.

According to recent reports, these percentages describe relative differences in risk between groups, not the absolute probability that an individual will die from cardiovascular disease. Because the research was observational, the findings also cannot demonstrate that choosing one alcoholic beverage over another directly changes a person's risk.

"Our findings help clarify previously mixed evidence on low to moderate alcohol consumption," Chen noted. "These findings can help refine guidance, emphasizing that the health risks of alcohol depend not only on the amount of alcohol consumed, but also on the type of beverage. Even low to moderate intake of spirits, beer, or cider is linked to higher mortality, while low to moderate intake of wine may carry lower risk.".

Why Might Wine Be Linked to Lower Heart Risks?

Researchers identified several possible explanations for the differences, including the chemical composition of wine and the habits of people who drink it.

Industry observers note that red wine contains polyphenols, naturally occurring compounds found in plants that can have antioxidant properties. Antioxidants help counter certain chemical reactions involving unstable molecules that can damage cells. Some polyphenols have been investigated for potential benefits to blood vessels and cardiovascular function.

These compounds could contribute to the associations observed in wine drinkers, although the study did not establish that they were responsible for the lower mortality risk.

Another possible explanation involves how and when people drink.

Industry observers note that wine is more commonly consumed alongside meals, and wine drinkers often report healthier diets and lifestyle habits. Drinking wine may therefore be associated with other behaviors that support cardiovascular health.

Sources indicate that beer, cider, and spirits, on the other hand, are more frequently consumed outside of meals. In this study, people who favored these beverages also tended to have poorer overall diet quality and other lifestyle factors associated with increased health risks.

Such differences make it difficult to separate the effects of the alcohol itself from the characteristics and habits of the people consuming it.

"Taken together, these factors suggest that the type of alcohol, how it is consumed, and the associated lifestyle behaviors all contribute to the observed differences in mortality risk," Chen stated.

What the Findings Mean for Alcohol and Health.

To make their comparisons more reliable, the researchers statistically adjusted their analyses for numerous factors that might influence mortality. These included age and other demographic characteristics, socioeconomic circumstances, lifestyle behaviors, and cardiometabolic health.

Sources indicate that cardiometabolic factors include conditions and measurements related to heart and metabolic health, such as blood pressure, blood sugar regulation, and cholesterol levels. The analyses also accounted for family histories of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and cancer.

Even with these adjustments, the researchers emphasized several important limitations.

According to recent reports, because the study was observational, it could identify associations between alcohol consumption and mortality but could not prove that particular beverages caused better or worse outcomes. Other differences between participants may have influenced the findings despite the statistical adjustments.

Alcohol intake was also measured through questionnaires completed when participants first entered the study. That information depended on participants accurately reporting their own drinking habits, and it did not capture changes in consumption during the years that followed.

Another consideration is that UK Biobank participants tend to be healthier than the general population. This could limit how well the findings apply to other groups of people.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers suggested that high-quality randomized trials could provide stronger evidence about the health effects of different drinking patterns. Such studies would help clarify whether the observed differences reflect the beverages themselves or other factors associated with their consumption.

Nevertheless, the enormous study population and more than 13 years of average follow-up provide considerable statistical strength. By examining specific types of alcohol, different levels of consumption, and multiple causes of death, the research offers a more detailed picture of alcohol's potential health risks than many earlier investigations.

The findings highlight an key distinction: while heavy drinking is consistently associated with harmful health outcomes, the relationships observed at lower consumption levels may depend on beverage choice, drinking habits, and broader lifestyle patterns.

In a recent development, for now, the apparent advantage among wine drinkers should not be interpreted as a reason to start drinking wine for heart health. The evidence points to a complex relationship between alcohol and mortality, rather than proving that any alcoholic drink offers protection.

Ziyue Li presented the study, "Alcohol Use at Mid-Life and All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality," at ACC.26.

Breaking: Holiday Gift Guide 2026

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, few additions to the latest Dungeons & Dragons rules pack as much punch and value as this new expansion, focusing on ways to develop further and evolve the use of magic across your tabletop gaming sessions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that with the holiday gift-giving season upon us, it’s time to think about the gaming fans in your life and find the ideal present to brighten their day. And if you’re the gamer in the family, we always encourage you to circle relevant items in the coming pages and leave your magazine open in hard-to-miss locations around the house. We’ve scoured dozens of tech products, tabletop games, collectibles, and more to select and highlight some of the coolest items we found this year.

We recommended the Board shortly after its launch, but with its expanded game library and lower price than first-adopter rates, this holiday season is an ideal time to make the leap. This family-friendly platform features original games that sit comfortably between the digital and physical divide. The horizontally placed screen shows the backdrop of one of the several included games, or the sold-separately add-on games that have popped in since launch. Each game has its own real physical play pieces that interact with the action onscreen, often in innovative and charming ways. Think of it as the best of both worlds between board games and video games, and you’ll get what they’re shooting for here. $399.

According to recent reports, few additions to the latest Dungeons & Dragons rules pack as much punch and value as this new expansion, focusing on ways to develop further and evolve the use of magic across your tabletop gaming sessions. New subclasses, spells, creatures, magical items, and factions add thoughtful, intriguing options for both players looking to play someone new and DMs hunting for new story hooks and challenges. $50.

In a recent development, if you’re as excited as we are about this month’s celebration of the Tomb Raider legacy (see p. 40), this centerpiece statue is an ideal fit for your collection. Standing roughly nine inches in height, Lara is poised for exploration in her original classic garb. The sculpt strikes a perfect balance between crisp detail and stylistic presentation, in line with that early version of the character; the metallic blue motorcycle paint is especially striking. $250.

According to recent reports, for players longing for the glory days of stand-up arcade games, it’s hard to beat Arcade 1Up’s approach. The team’s sturdy cabinets look and sound great as a marquee feature of your game room. The latest Outrun machine features much of the original display art, a bright 19-inch screen, and responsive gas and brake pedals as you steer around those tight corners. Sega has packed in OutRun, Turbo OutRun, OutRunners, and Power Drift. If old-school racing isn’t your thing, look for cabinets that run the gamut from Pac-Man to Joust to Claw Machines. $629.99.

The long-running Nendoroid figures continue to be an attractive but still affordable choice for building collections across numerous fan-favorite series. There are somewhere around 2000 characters at this point! Fresh entries like the Genshin Impact collection make a strong case for the line. The look is chibi, the quality is excellent, poseability is high, and customizable face and accessory parts let you change up your display over time. $46.

We’ve previously sung the praises of Libernovo’s versatile approach to an ergonomic gaming chair, which includes a lumbar stretch functionality, a steady recline option for comfortable pushback without sudden shifts, and dynamically adjusting parts as you move through your day. The Maxis line does all that, but addresses one of the fundamental problems for at least some people with the original – it wasn’t major enough. With features like a wider base and longer headrest reach, the Maxis aims to provide the same comfort to the players who are tall or wide enough to need the extra breathing room. $1119.

Privacy around smart glasses has been a major point of contention as wearable tech continues to expand. Even G2s have a clear answer to that issue by consciously leaving out a camera. Instead, these glasses focus on productivity and specific tasks, like real-time translation into 35 languages, in-lens teleprompters for presentations, and calendar notifications – all presented in a readable display that is largely invisible from the outside. $600.

In a recent development, if you’re the player on your team who likes to have easy access to soundboards and real-time voice changing, the Key Pocket could be just the ticket. This small device straps onto your phone for mobile play, but it’s also compatible with consoles, Discord, Twitch, or just about any place you want to tweak audio on the fly. A free tier gives you access to some voice-changing and sounds, while a separate subscription opens up hundreds of thousands of additional options. But be warned: we can’t help you after your friends abandon you for that baby voice you won’t stop using. $99.

According to recent reports, the question of the best bang for your buck in modern consoles has become extraordinarily complicated, especially as tech prices have soared in recent years. There’s no right answer, but Sony’s high-end machine walks the line of offering extremely high-tier performance without escalating to even higher-priced gaming PCs. Higher and more consistent frame rates than on standard PS5, advanced ray tracing, and an increasing number of games that feature enhanced PSSR image options all add up to a better gaming experience, if you’re ready to make the significant price jump. $900.

In a recent development, if the gamer in your life is looking for a stylish, understated way to express their love of the hobby, Anicorn’s designer watch collaboration with PlayStation could be a standout option. Available in black and a slick silver/white combo, the minimalist timepiece includes the familiar face buttons of Sony’s controller encased in an oil-injection display so they slowly and freely float across the watch as you move. $250.

According to recent reports, it’s a safe bet you’ve at least seen the popular Shashibo puzzle cubes by this point. We’ve been fans of their brain-teasing, fidgety fun for some time. Battle Shapes takes the core concept – reshaping the box into various distinct magnetically-locked shapes – and extends it into a timed game experience, playable solo or head-to-head. By targeting specific shapes, you significantly improve your speed with the toy, and scannable QR codes on the cards offer clear tutorials for each shape so you can prep for competition. $50.

While the vast majority of gamers looking for good personal audio are going to be okay with a larger set of cans over their ears, We know more than a few players for whom that’s a definite no – for comfort, awareness of surrounding sounds, or other reasons. The Arc 5 earbuds aim to solve for that, with an over-ear design that feels extremely comfortable. And because they sit on the ear, you can still hear what’s going on around you. While that limits some aspects of the final sound quality, the inclusion of THX certification, Dolby Atmos optimization, and Dynamic Bass Enhancement helps to ensure audio is still very strong. $230.

Across Lego’s many recent themes, Tolkien’s legendarium has offered some stellar sets. The largest yet is the capital of Gondor, with an astonishing 8,278 pieces and a height of roughly two feet. The castle/city build is impressive, featuring tons of interesting angles and turns. The finished product aims to offer the best of both worlds in presentation – a microscale representation of the front façade and a reverse minifigure-scale Hall of Kings. We especially like the inclusion of Denethor’s cherry tomatoes. $650.

The original Azul is often cited as a foundational entry in modern board gaming. The “Kids” versions of celebrated titles aren’t always a sure bet, but this one holds up to scrutiny. Azul Kids lowers the complexity threshold but keeps the foundational strategic thinking. Players lay out uniquely shaped tiles into mosaic frameworks in colorful, appealing patterns; the basic concept of the original inspiration is clear, and kids as young as five can grasp and enjoy the fun. $25.

Industry observers note that many corners of the collecting world have embraced the fun (and frequent despair) of blind boxes, where you never know exactly who you’ll get in a given series. Funism has a strong track record for quality, offering adorable smaller figures like their latest line of Evangelion collectibles. Each figure stands nearly four inches and features both human characters and mecha. You can buy singles and roll the dice, or purchase larger sets with a no-duplicates guarantee, which can save a lot of heartache if you’re trying to line your whole shelf. $21.

Sources indicate that if you’re going to spring for a high-end keyboard for PC gaming, it’s vital that you like the feel of the keys. The slightly smaller overall 75% size profile of this Blackwidow has no impact on the great feel of typing – a clear highlight for the unit. The customizable, colored backlights are also a big selling point, as is the side command dial and built-in OLED display, which can be tweaked to show PC performance, GIFs, lighting brightness, and more. It’s a strong contender in a crowded field, and justifies its price with both comfort and customizability. $300.

Beautiful, vibrant art and a refreshing take on the classic area-control board game genre are the two strongest reasons to take a close look at Wroth. Players control one of five races vying for supremacy across a conflict-ridden peninsula. Factions are asymmetric, so everyone has unique capabilities, and that adds significant replayability. Players roll and draft dice, allowing distinct actions that move the game forward. And move it does; unlike many games of this ilk, Wroth can be learned quickly and played to completion in a little over an hour. $65.

Console and computer hardware prices are skyrocketing with no sign of slowing, and perhaps as a result, retro gaming handhelds are gaining popularity. Many quality devices are available, but what sets the Evercade Nexus apart is its officially licensed game cartridges. Imagine the nostalgic joy of a Game Boy, but with a cartridge that includes both Banjo-Kazooie and Tooie. The cartridge boxes even include manuals. For fans of physical media, Evercade Nexus is a great option. $199.

This tiny USB-C plug-in (with included USB-A adapter) solves a bunch of audio challenges in one uniform device. It offers high-resolution Bluetooth transmission on iPhone, high-bitrate audio transmission to compatible LDAC headphones, enables high-quality Bluetooth output from your PC, and even low-latency Bluetooth audio on PS5 and Switch. In short, it takes a huge number of products with a USB port and ensures a dynamic Bluetooth audio connection with relative ease. $99.

Industry observers note that the original MV6 is a familiar sight on streams thanks to its clear voice reproduction and overall ease of use. Shure has built on that success with the Gen 2, offering an excellent standalone mic that doesn’t break the bank. Available in black or white, the Gen 2 features a handy auto-level mode that keeps volume even as you adjust your own amplitude, an adjustable denoiser for your space, a longer cable for out-of-the-box convenience, and three presets for plug-and-play use. In short, it’s an excellent choice if you want great performance without needing an audio engineering degree. $169.

XR Glasses are still fighting for awareness, but once you try them, it’s easy to see why the concept is on the rise. Viture’s Pro 2 makes an impressive case for adoption, with a competitive price point, comfortable wear, and a giant 146-inch screen that floats in front of your face for gaming or work on your PC or phone. The display is crisp, bright, and impressive, even as the glasses are light and easy to use. With a mobile dock mini (sold separately), you can even snap onto a Switch 2 with ease and start playing instantly. $299.

Role-playing gamers have several excellent universal systems to pick between when considering a story or campaign idea that might fall outside traditional genre staples. Among many good options, Cypher stands out as one of the very best. The system uses a rules-light, narrative-focused approach that prioritizes player-driven storytelling across everything from hard sci-fi to superheroes to intrigue- driven espionage. This is the corebook that’s needed to run and play the full system; additional books only add options. $50.

As gamers have continually migrated toward personal audio that can rock amazing sound without disturbing the whole house, high-end premium headphones have become a dangerously competitive space. Turtle Beach meets that challenge head-on, with a robust option that sounds beautiful in use. The Stealth Pro II boasts the slick ability to wirelessly switch between different devices, which is awesome if you’re one of those players who regularly jumps between platforms to play your favorite titles. Like the whole category, it’s a lot to spend on a headset, but Dolby Atmos, active noise cancellation, and 60mm dual drivers all add up to a powerful argument. $300.

With an increasing number of top-tier console and PC games like Resident Evil Village, No Man’s Sky, and Dead Cells now available on iOS, not to mention the consistent quality of Apple Arcade, Apple phones remain the best mobile platform for gaming. The 18 Pro Max phone has implemented a number of tweaks that strengthen the platform, including higher memory, much faster graphics processing, impressive HDR performance, and notably improved battery life, all adding up to a gaming experience that is working hard to justify your playtime when away from home. Starting at $1299.

It has been revealed that steelSeries is best known for its strong audio line-up, but its push into premium-tier controllers exhibits a similar flair for quality and usability. The new Aeon Pro has a lot to recommend it as your go-to Xbox, PC, or mobile choice. The two included batteries (one of which can always be charging in the dock) ensure essentially unlimited playtime. The full-pull or hair triggers and buttons are clicky and satisfying, and the Hall Effect thumbsticks are built to minimize any drift. Textured handgrips and overall heft are ideal. And an onboard OLED lets you adjust profiles and button assignments, switch between platforms, and check battery at a glance. $260.

Valve’s pricey VR headset isn’t a revolution in the medium, but the manufacturer has been invested in the technology since its inception. As a result, the Steam Frame is a very good, very comfortable headset. Like its competition, the Quest, its best use is playing games locally on the headset, and Steam’s library is vast and interesting. Wireless connected play to a powerful PC is also well done, but right now the included Wireless Adapter is not fully compatible with the Steam Machine – a baffling limitation we were shocked to confirm. VR is an expensive sub-hobby within video games, but Steam Frame is among the best ways to explore and enjoy it. $1059.

Sources indicate that many of the coolest “gaming lights” focus on the flexibility and fun of bright RGB customization. While we’re fans of that aesthetic, it leaves others out in the cold who might want something a bit more natural. The Elements hex panels feature a natural wood-inspired panel, customizable “scenes” like a campfire glow, and can react to both music and touch, with adjustable ambient white light to keep the vibe relaxed. $200.

Kyle Hilliard contributed to this article.

Sources indicate that bad signal or dead zones? Download your issues before you leave and read anywhere.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 might take players to a fictional version of Florida, but its success is apparently something the British government is more than happy to claim! After more than 10 years of anticipation, Rockstar’s latest blockbuster has finally arrived in the UK, and Downing Street has already found a reason to celebrate.

Oh, but there's just one small problem: Prime Minister Andy Burnham won't be joining the party, as his schedule is apparently a little too packed for a trip to Vice City.

Speaking to reporters on Thursday (thanks, The Independent), a Downing Street spokesperson described Rockstar Games as a "British success story made in Edinburgh," adding that many fans were already saying GTA 6 had been worth the wait.

In a recent development, when asked whether Burnham would be playing the game himself, however, the response was considerably less enthusiastic: "His diary is very full. He won't be playing it.".

It's a pretty amusing contrast, especially considering just how many people in the UK have been making room in their schedules for Rockstar's fresh release! But hey, I get him – we’re talking about an experience that easily will get hold of 100+ hours of your life.

Although GTA 6 is set in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida, a significant part of the game's development took place in Scotland. Rockstar North, the studio responsible for much of the franchise's development, is based in Edinburgh, making the government's description of the game as a British success story more than just a bit of patriotic enthusiasm.

When asked whether Burnham would be playing the game himself, however, the response was considerably less enthusiastic: "His diary is very full. He won't be playing it.".

The studio has been one of the UK's most recognizable names in the gaming industry for years, and GTA 6's launch is another major achievement for the country's game development scene. After all, it's not every day that one of the most anticipated entertainment releases in the world comes from a studio with such a strong presence in the UK, right?

Still, Burnham's absence from the player count might be a little disappointing for anyone hoping to see the Prime Minister share his first impressions of Vice City. At least Downing Street has made its position clear: the game is worth celebrating, even if its leader won't be playing it.

While Burnham apparently has more pressing matters to attend to, plenty of other people in the UK have found a way to squeeze GTA 6 into their day! A poll commissioned by Uswitch earlier this month estimated that around 2.8 million UK adults would play the game on launch day alone, with many expected to take annual leave or even call in sick to work.

According to recent reports, the game's arrival has also prompted schools to remind students that its release isn't an excuse to skip lessons. GTA 6 carries an 18 age rating, and some schools have even introduced prize draws for vouchers among students who attend classes, hoping to keep attendance numbers up during the launch frenzy!

It has been revealed that honestly, it's hard to imagine a better illustration of just how massive this release has become. Rockstar has managed to turn a video game launch into an event significant enough to reach Downing Street, spark discussions about school attendance, and even inspire millions of people to rearrange their schedules.

Burnham might not be joining Jason and Lucia on their adventures, but at least he can take comfort in knowing that a major British studio is behind one of the biggest games of the year. And, judging by the number of people taking the day off, his diary might be the only thing keeping him away from Vice City.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG.
  • According to recent reports, as recently revealed, the latest experience rolls out today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT.
  • This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

According to recent reports, as recently revealed, the latest experience rolls out today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the initiative is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as swiftly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

The Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

Sources indicate that the Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two latest additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that automakers love to lean on nostalgia.
  • It has been revealed that fullGood made an unexpected appearance at the Los Angeles auto show, where it is looking to find a partner to help bring its retro-themed vehicles to the United States.
  • Sources indicate that now FullGood wants to make a return to the United States.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that automakers love to lean on nostalgia. Whether it’s a upcoming paint job inspired by an old race car, or reviving a classic nameplate for a new model, utilizing a rich history can be an easy way to grab customers’ attention. But what if a manufacturer leaned on the heritage of other automakers? That’s where FullGood Motor, a Chinese company that builds modern plug-in hybrids inspired by classic cars, steps in, and FullGood now wants to break into the U.S. market.

It has been revealed that fullGood made an unexpected appearance at the Los Angeles auto show, where it is looking to find a partner to help bring its retro-themed vehicles to the United States. The manufacturer was formed back in 1995 as a motorcycle business called Loose Motor, and didn’t get into the automobile business until 2009. In fact, the pivot to cars was initially based out of a factory in California, before the company moved its operations to Beijing, China, in 2018, adopting the FullGood name in 2022.

See all results for used cars for sale near 07011.

Sources indicate that now FullGood wants to make a return to the United States. The manufacturer says business is strong in China, where its factory has a 100,000-unit-per-year capacity, hence the desire to expand. We spoke with the company’s vice president, Erelly Cai, at the LA auto show to understand a bit more about the brand’s desire to come to the U.S. and the potential hurdles it might face.

Recent findings suggest that the tech giant knows it can’t enter the U.S. market alone, especially in an era where regulations make it nigh on impossible for Chinese automakers to import their vehicles. FullGood acknowledges this challenge and is in Los Angeles seeking to talk with investors and potential American manufacturing and distribution partners.

It has been revealed that the plan is to export vehicles from China in component form, and then complete final assembly in the U.S. The vehicles would then be sold and registered under its American partners’ brand. It also wants to develop more vehicles directly inspired by midcentury American design.

FullGood brought one of its cars to the show, a seven-seat van named the Summer that is undoubtedly inspired by the Volkswagen Type 2, better known as the Microbus. Like all of its models, the Summer uses a plug-in hybrid powertrain. The Summer pairs a turbocharged 1.5-liter engine with electric motors from Wuling, a large and well-established Chinese automaker, and a 28-kWh battery from CATL. The front-wheel-drive powertrain produces a combined 325 hp, with electric-only driving range listed at 93 miles and total range at 497 miles. The Summer costs the equivalent of $49,000 at current exchange rates.

See all results for used cars for sale near 07011.

It has been revealed that cai said that the manufacturer would likely use the same powertrain if it manages to introduce its vehicles to the U.S. market, with the bigger obstacle being the car’s software. The U.S. Department of Commerce’s Connected Vehicle Rule bans foreign-made cars that feature certain connected software and hardware from China and Russia. Some companies that import from China, such as Volvo, have been granted an exemption, while others, like Polestar, have been banned from the U.S.

In a recent development, fullGood hopes the LA show can help it find a partner, so “maybe we can solve the problem together,” Cai mentioned. The idea would be to replace the software with a latest setup for the U.S. market, while keeping things like the chassis, powertrain, and interior trimmings unchanged. Along with the Summer, FullGood’s current planned lineup includes the Dolphin, which looks like a C1 Corvette; the Rocket, which emulates the 1959 Cadillac Eldorado; and the HotRod, which looks like a Ford Model A.

Industry observers note that if FullGood manages to find a partner and bring their cars to the United States, it imagines capturing a market of buyers who are nostalgic for vehicles from their past. “They have their childhood memories,” Cai said, with FullGood’s vehicles helping to “bring those memories back.” While FullGood is still a long way from getting its cars to our shores, they certainly provide a different attitude than the current crop of vehicles sold in the U.S., with their cheery, whimsical designs, and while the barrier to getting here is high, we’re curious to see where FullGood’s Los Angeles appearance takes the oddball company.

In a recent development, caleb Miller began blogging about cars at 13 years old, and he realized his dream of writing for a car magazine after graduating from Carnegie Mellon University and joining the Car and Driver team. He loves quirky and obscure autos, aiming to one day own something bizarre like a Nissan S-Cargo, and is an avid motorsports fan.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that as marijuana becomes more widely available and accepted, researchers are uncovering vital questions about its effects on mental health.
  • Published in the Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs, the research found that adults with cannabis use disorder had 57% higher odds of reporting suicidal thoughts compared with those without the condition.
  • In a recent development, the findings come from an analysis of more than 415,000 American adults who participated in the National Survey on Drug Use and Health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that as marijuana becomes more widely available and accepted, researchers are uncovering vital questions about its effects on mental health. A major new study suggests that people who struggle to control their cannabis use face a substantially greater likelihood of experiencing suicidal thoughts.

Published in the Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs, the research found that adults with cannabis use disorder had 57% higher odds of reporting suicidal thoughts compared with those without the condition. Despite major shifts in marijuana laws and public attitudes, this troubling association remained remarkably consistent over a decade.

In a recent development, the findings come from an analysis of more than 415,000 American adults who participated in the National Survey on Drug Use and Health. Researchers examined data collected between 2014 and 2023, a period when cannabis became increasingly accessible across the United States.

It has been revealed that "What surprised me most was not that cannabis use disorder was associated with suicidal thoughts, but that this association did not appear to strengthen over time," said lead author Tosin Philip Oyetunji, MPH, a doctoral student in public health at the University of California, Merced. "[Yet,] it remains an important mental health concern that deserves attention.".

Cannabis and Suicidal Thoughts Show a Persistent Link.

The connection between cannabis use disorder and suicidal thinking was observed across different age groups, sexes, and racial and ethnic backgrounds. However, women and younger adults revealed particularly elevated risks.

Importantly, the association remained even after researchers accounted for depression, psychological distress, and other factors that could influence mental health outcomes.

Sources indicate that the consistency of the results was especially notable given how dramatically the cannabis landscape has changed. Recreational marijuana is now legal in half of U.S. states, and cannabis products have become increasingly potent. These developments have raised concerns among public health experts about whether broader access might contribute to worsening mental health.

Yet the study offers some reassurance on that particular question. Sidra Goldman-Mellor, PhD, a professor of public health at UC Merced and the study's senior author, noted that the association between cannabis use disorder and suicidal thoughts did not become stronger during the 10 years examined.

"Suicidal ideation does not seem to have increased among people with cannabis use disorder, despite all this legal and social change," explained Goldman-Mellor. Yet, "people with cannabis use disorder are still at a very substantially increased likelihood of experiencing serious suicidal thoughts, and that's not something that is widely understood.".

Why Cannabis Use Disorder Matters.

The researchers stress that these findings should not be interpreted as evidence that everyone who uses marijuana faces the same elevated risk.

The study focused specifically on cannabis use disorder, a condition in which people have difficulty controlling their marijuana consumption even when it causes problems in their lives. Someone with the disorder may continue using cannabis despite harmful consequences or repeated attempts to cut back.

This distinction is crucial because problematic cannabis use differs from occasional or otherwise nonproblematic consumption.

The findings also do not establish that cannabis use disorder directly causes suicidal thoughts. Because the research identified an association rather than a cause-and-effect relationship, it cannot determine whether problematic cannabis use contributes to suicidal thinking, whether underlying mental health difficulties contribute to both conditions, or whether other factors help explain the connection.

Nevertheless, the results point to a significant mental health concern that deserves greater recognition, particularly among people seeking help for problematic cannabis use.

Researchers Urge Greater Mental Health Screening.

One practical implication is that health care professionals should look beyond cannabis consumption itself when evaluating patients with cannabis use disorder.

Rather than focusing exclusively on depression or substance use symptoms, clinicians may benefit from asking patients directly about suicidal thoughts as part of a broader mental health assessment. This could help identify people who need additional care but whose struggles might otherwise remain unnoticed.

"Someone seeking help for cannabis use disorder may also be experiencing suicidal thoughts that are not immediately apparent," mentioned Oyetunji. "The goal is not to assume that everyone with cannabis use disorder is suicidal but to identify those who may need additional assessment, treatment, or support.".

According to recent reports, the study arrives at a time when marijuana is increasingly viewed as a relatively low-risk substance. Public perceptions have shifted considerably, and negative attitudes toward cannabis have declined alongside expanding legalization and social acceptance.

In a recent development, however, these changes have not eliminated the mental health challenges associated with cannabis use disorder. Even though the strength of the association with suicidal thoughts did not increase over the study period, the elevated odds remained substantial.

The researchers suggest that health care providers, policymakers, and community organizations can play an important role by improving awareness, identifying vulnerable individuals, and making appropriate mental health support more accessible.

As attitudes toward marijuana continue to evolve, the findings serve as a reminder that the needs of people experiencing problematic cannabis use should remain a public health priority.

Said Oyetunji, "As cannabis becomes more accessible and socially accepted, we should ensure that the people struggling with its use are not overlooked.".

Recent findings suggest that in a statement posted yesterday, Killing Floor developers Tripwire Interactive have announced that the studio is laying off 36 "talented" internal staff as part of a "workforce reduction". The job cuts come 16 months after the release of Killing Floor 3 (which James didn't care for), and within hours of unrelated yet equally dispiriting redunancies at Skydance Games.

Tripwire's announcement claims that this was "not an easy decision, but unfortunately a necessary one for the organisation," adding that "these are truly great people who are exceptional at their roles, and we will help support these individuals with compassion and dignity during this transition." There's a small hope in me that this might mean helping those affected find newly introduced jobs rapidly, though it's hard to stay optimistic when mass layoffs in games development have become such a regular occurrence.

Despite this post primarily being about the loss of 36 livelihoods, Tripwire are quick to reassure fans that Killing Floor 3's post-launch updates remain in active development, as does their comedy shark-action sequel Maneater 2. The studio "remain committed to our awesome community", they say; apparently just not to their awesome employees.

This news also arrives just days after Tripwire expanded its publishing business to support small indie developers, and less than a year after its last round of layoffs in March. Tripwire also happens to have been acquired by layoff extraordinaire corporation Embracer in 2022, just for some relevant context.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It’s one thing to see the Tesla Roadster through your smartphone screen; it’s another thing to see it about six feet away.
  • Sources indicate that being in the same room as a Bugatti EB110 is about as common as being in the same room as Sir Anthony Hopkins.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if you’re in downtown Los Angeles now through November 29 and want to get an up-close-and-personal look at some cool cars, head over to the convention center to see what’s poppin’ at the annual auto show. However, if you don’t have time to make the trip—or you’re nowhere near L.A.—and want to see the best cars that this year’s event had to offer, we've got you covered. While the 2026 L.A. auto show was short on major debuts or futuristic concepts, it hosted several headline-catching cars as well as multiple highly anticipated new models.

It’s one thing to see the Tesla Roadster through your smartphone screen; it’s another thing to see it about six feet away. While we’re highly skeptical that Tesla will ever publicly sell the thruster-equipped version that flew through the air and did a barrel roll, it’s more likely that a similar-looking, street-legal version will eventually reach production. Haters gonna hate, but the Roadster looks pretty damn cool, like Lamborghini designer Fabrizio Giugiaro was hired to style his version of the Lotus Esprit S1 that James Bond drove in The Spy Who Loved Me. Consider us shaken, not stirred.

Sources indicate that being in the same room as a Bugatti EB110 is about as common as being in the same room as Sir Anthony Hopkins. Like meeting the actor who famously played Hannibal Lecter, meeting one of the most iconic supercars ever made is unnerving. Now, you may have noticed that this example isn’t exactly all original; instead, it has been modified by Phiaro Inc., and it features a custom widebody kit as well as a chameleon-like paint job. The best part? Its modifications are completely reversible. Let’s just say it drew a crowd.

In a recent development, genesis is going after the throats of luxury stalwarts like BMW, Mercedes-Benz and—dare we say—Bentley with the fresh GV90. The one you see here is the top-of-the-line Neolun model, and its most distinctive feature is these gigantic coach doors. Inside are four VIP-grade seats that treat passengers to an opulent cabin awash in rich materials and front seats that swivel 180 degrees to create a mobile lounge (this configuration is only accessible when the 657-hp EV is parked). The GV90 Neolun also has a veneer wood floor and 24-inch wheels that remind us of the iconic monoblock wheels made famous by Mercedes-AMG and Brabus. Few SUVs turn our heads, but Genesis appears to have another game-changer on its metaphorical hands.

Toyota Crown Signia GT-S Concept.

We spotted this beautiful wagon-like Toyota Crown Signia from across the convention center’s south hall. Among a sea of generic crossovers, this low-slung longroof is an ode to an age when most Americans didn’t lust after the elevated seating position of a semi-truck. Of course, if you haven’t noticed, this isn’t exactly a production-spec Crown Signia. If you read our recent SEMA coverage, you may recognize it as the GT-S concept. Along with being lowered by five inches and wearing flared fenders that resemble the Mustang GTD, it has custom one-off coil-over dampers, 21-inch HRE wheels, and brakes from a Lexus RX500h F Sport. To all that, we say, “Hell yeah, brother!”.

In a recent development, let’s take a break from the world of flying cars, Bugattis, and fanciful electric SUVs to enjoy something that most people can afford: the fresh eighth-generation Hyundai Elantra. If its disorienting front lighting, heavily creased bodywork, and broad haunches intimidate you, we’re sure there’s a safer-looking alternative in Toyota’s showroom. But whatever you may think about the new Elantra’s styling, it definitely attracts attention. And Hyundai is hoping it’ll do just that to new customers who are looking to join the brand’s family tree. The nonhybrid version seen here draws power from a humble 147-hp four-cylinder engine, but the lineup will add a more powerful hybrid model sometime next year. While pricing is still TBD, we expect that it’ll cost around $25,000 to own the most interesting car in your cul-de-sac.

Ram 1500 Rumble Bee Foose Edition.

Recent findings suggest that if you’ve ever watched an episode of Overhaulin’, a TV show that lasted for 10 seasons on TLC, then you’ve heard of custom car designer Chip Foose. Now, he has teamed up with Fox Factory Vehicles to create this even more muscular version of the new Ram 1500 Rumble Bee street truck. Along with unique wheels and body graphics, the interior has been restyled with diamond-stitched seats and Foose branding. The truck itself has a lowered ride height with an aftermarket coil-over suspension, and its supercharged V-8 is available with either 705 or 1000 horsepower. That’s a lot of horsies, and they’ll cost customers a lot of cash, with the Rumble Bee Foose Edition starting at $154,990.

This was one of the few concept cars at the show, but the Acura Nexera was first revealed back in August during Monterey Car Week. Still, the futuristic concept is really cool to see in person, especially with its dramatic glass canopy. Plus, how many times have you seen an Acura with butterfly doors? While the Nexera doesn’t preview an upcoming production model, it does provide a glimpse of Acura’s next-generation design language. Will the newly introduced 2028 RDX feature an active rear spoiler, carbon-fiber accents, and lighting that glows through the bodywork? Probably not. However, we can expect to see some of the Nexera concept’s interesting styling influence the brand’s next-gen compact SUV.

Acura Integra Type S Heritage Edition.

It has been revealed that if you’re old enough to remember Acura’s legendary DC2 Integra Type R, you’ll definitely appreciate this upcoming Integra Type S Heritage Edition. Not only does its Blazing Phoenix Yellow call more attention to itself than Substantial Bird starring in an old-timey picture show, but it also honors the OG Type R, which also wore a shade of Phoenix Yellow. The modern-day throwback sport compact packs the same 320-hp turbo four and six-speed manual as other models, but this one alone has copper-colored wheels and a titanium shift knob from the Honda Civic Type R. To get one in your driveway, you’ll need to be lucky enough to score one of the 700 limited copies for the U.S. market, but the asking price is a reasonable $58,995.

Have you been waiting for Dodge to stuff a Hemi V-8 in the upcoming Charger? Well, you’re going to have to keep waiting for a while. However, if you’ve been hoping that the Brotherhood of Muscle will make a gas-powered Charger that’s set up for quick lap times, the new Super Bee variant should help you scratch that itch. Along with exclusive aero bits, stronger brakes, and wider summer tires, this track-focused Charger features an enhanced high-output Hurricane twin-turbo 3.0-liter straight-six, which is good for 600 horsepower (50 more than normal). The reimagined “Super Bee” logo on the rear quarter panel is one way to separate it from its siblings, but it also has an entirely different front clip that features new headlights and more open space to inhale engine-cooling air. If you’re wondering how much it costs, so are we, so stay tuned.

Sources indicate that like many of you, this was our first time seeing the fresh Chevy Silverado 1500’s new off-road-focused ZR2 variant. It’s a major truck, so big that we initially thought it was the HD version. Among the many changes to the newest generation of Chevy’s bestselling full-size pickup truck are all-new small-block V-8s. The ZR2 seen here is powered by a 481-hp 6.6-liter that helps churn massive all-terrain tires, which now stand 35 inches tall for the first time on a half-ton Silverado. The Ford F-150 Raptor-rivaling ZR2’s other party tricks include trick Multimatic DSSV spool-valve dampers. Inside, it includes GM’s first use of forged carbon fiber (neat!). If you want the most badass version, you’ll want to opt for the Bison Edition that adds beadlock-capable wheels, unique bumpers, and even more underbody armor. The cost of admission for the regular ZR2 is just under $80K, while the Bison starts even higher.

In a recent development, eric Stafford’s automobile addiction began before he could walk, and it has fueled his passion to write news, reviews, and more for Car and Driver since 2016. His aspiration growing up was to become a millionaire with a Jay Leno–like car collection. Apparently, getting rich is harder than social-media influencers make it seem, so he avoided financial success entirely to become an automotive journalist and drive new cars for a living. After earning a journalism degree at Central Michigan University and working at a daily newspaper, the years of basically burning money on failed project cars and lemon-flavored jalopies finally paid off when Car and Driver hired him. His garage currently includes a 2010 Acura RDX, a manual '97 Chevy Camaro Z/28, and a '90 Honda CRX Si.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In their (slightly belated) upcoming years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are at the moment working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

In a recent development, this, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

It has been revealed that understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s upcoming ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we plan for today, tomorrow, and the future.”.

According to recent reports, as for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of newly introduced Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post notes that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Recent findings suggest that future releases, of course, include latest The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.).

GTA’s Tool Choice Over Milwaukee Gives DeWalt Fans Bragging Rights

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A big part of what’s giving Grand Theft Auto 6 its incredible hypnotic power over a statistically-significant portion of the gaming public is its gigantic, intricately-designed world.
  • According to recent reports, early in the game, after receiving word that one of the game’s protagonists, Lucia, is coming back from prison, our other lead, Jason, can work to fix up their bungalow home in order to preemptively improve his relationship level with her.
  • A certain subset of players couldn’t help but notice that the tools Jason uses when fixing the walls and roof are colored a distinct shade of yellow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A big part of what’s giving Grand Theft Auto 6 its incredible hypnotic power over a statistically-significant portion of the gaming public is its gigantic, intricately-designed world. There are so, so many details to uncover all over the place if you take a moment to stop and look for them, and I’m not just talking about Bigfoot hanging out in the swamps or the many varieties of bird flying around. There are lots of little details that subtly inform aspects of the characters’ personalities and interests, including, apparently, the particular brands of power tools they prefer.

According to recent reports, early in the game, after receiving word that one of the game’s protagonists, Lucia, is coming back from prison, our other lead, Jason, can work to fix up their bungalow home in order to preemptively improve his relationship level with her. This means undertaking a few assorted tasks like repainting and fixing the walls, re-shingling the roof, fixing the stairs, and so-forth.

A certain subset of players couldn’t help but notice that the tools Jason uses when fixing the walls and roof are colored a distinct shade of yellow. The brand printed on the tool may be different from real-life, but fans of hardware know the distinct iconography of DeWalt when they see it.

For those with no interest in power tools, DeWalt is one of the most prominent brands in the scene, manufacturing all of the usual implements like power drills, nail guns, circular saws, and all that other good stuff, usually powered by rechargeable battery packs. As is so often the case with this sort of thing, fans of DeWalt have something of an unofficial rivalry with fans of other major hardware brands, especially Milwaukee, whose tools are usually colored red.

During Jason’s various household repair chores, he uses a couple of power tools colored the same shade of yellow as DeWalt’s, both emblazoned with the logo “DEVICE.” Obviously, Rockstar can’t just use DeWalt’s actual logo in its game without its permission (though I have a feeling DeWalt would’ve loved it if given the opportunity), but the particular font that the “DEVICE” logo is printed in, particularly with the slightly smaller “E” before the “V,” is unmistakable. Looks like Jason is a DeWalt man, and fans on the DeWalt subreddit are holding this up as a victory over the likes of Milwaukee.

The particular font that the “DEVICE” logo is printed in, particularly with the slightly smaller “E” before the “V,” is unmistakable.

The particular implements that Jason uses seem to be at least partially inspired by real-life DeWalt tools. The driver he uses when fixing the walls is nearly identical to DeWalt’s 20V MAX 1/4 inch impact driver. The nail gun he uses to fix the fencing and roof doesn’t seem to have as close of a parallel, but it most closely-resembles the DeWalt 20V MAX XR brad nailer. That’s not a roofing-specific nailer, though, so either I’m wrong or Jason just doesn’t differentiate between nailer types. I’d believe either scenario.

While this may seem like a granular detail to hyperfixate on, as I mentioned, it’s just kind of fun to examine every aspect of this simulated world. In addition to what I mentioned before about a character’s hardware preferences, it’s also interesting to hold up these simulated knock-off brands next to the real world.

A big part of the long-established aesthetic of the GTA world is riffing on aspects of real life. It’s always been a very exaggerated setting, often exemplifying the absolute worst parts of modern society for both laughs and drama. The fictional state of Leonida is pretty much Florida if it was slightly worse, and the same goes for Vice City and Miami.

GTA has also parodied more than its fair share of real-life brands and corporations over its various entries, usually with much sillier, ruder names. Sprite becomes “Sprunk,” IKEA becomes “KRAPEA,” and Twitter becomes “Bleeter,” which I am sincerely happy did not change its name to “Blex” or something equally stupid since GTA 5.
